The job title is: Payer Analyst.Further details:
 
 
The Payer Analyst individual is assigned to the Revenue Cycle Management Product Management Content Intelligence team. The individual finds and analyzes health plans and payor websites for billing related information and enters selected information using a standardized data collection system and is responsible for setting up the website tracking and maintenance of the system that auto-tags relevant information contained in the content.  The individual assures, for each organization targeted that all are found and any relevant URLs and content are  are collected. 
 
Primary Duties/Responsibility 1:  Payer Content Research
  • Researching Payer websites for content related to Healthcare Revenue Cycle Management and Billing. (Claims, Authorizations, Remittance Advice) Sign up for relevant email list-serves when available. 
  • Take the lead to proactively identify, track and distribute notifications to appropriate audiences to ensure issues are addressed before there is any impact to our customers.
  • Identify new trends that impact the healthcare industry for potential in-scope expansion.
Primary Duties/Responsibility 2:  Website Tracking & Maintenance
  • Setup website tracking using “point & click” tools allowing for changes of websites to be identified.
  • Tracking maintenance – resolve any tracking errors that may arise.  Monitor all tracking to ensure the latest versions of URLs/PDFs are input on a routine basis
Primary Duties/Responsibility 3:  NLP Tagging Setup & Maintenance
  • Setup the payer information in a Natural Language Processing system that allows for tagging of internal identifiers and content based subscription topics.
  • Maintain payer set up by adding additional alternative labels as needed, i.e. when new tracking is added.
  • Must be able to analyze overall system set-up concept to successfully resolve over/under tagging issues as they arise
Primary Duties/Responsibility 4:  Curate Internal Notification & Bulletins
  • Monitor incoming subscriptions and change tracking of payer websites to ensure NLP and Subscription topics are being properly associated with the information.
  • Modify/split content into individual articles building internal “payer notices” to internal subscribers (There’s a lot of reading, copy & pasting.)
  • Must maintain high standard in out-going content to Audiences with proper grammar, spelling and layout of the information.
  • Maintain turn-around time performance standards to ensure timely release of information.
Primary Duties/Responsibility 5:  Platform Migration
  • Assist the team in migrating and testing above business processes to a new platform and start performing processes in new system.
  • The ability to take on projects while maintaining current work-load; verbalizing the need for assistance when/if needed.
The Payer Content Intelligence Analyst individual requires the ability to read and identify changes that need to be made to existing Claims Edits and Prior Auth policies as well as create internal bulletins based on their interpretation of the content. While the majority of the content is notifying internal teams of the website or subscription changes the written communication needs to be concise and accurate when documenting policy changes. 

Preferred Qualification/s:
  • The ideal candidate is experienced in healthcare billing  with knowledge of managed care/payor/healthcare insurance companies who understands and has worked with medical policies, prior authorization, or utilization review.  Ability to comprehensively search the internet for payor content and accurate transcribe data to a prepared template is required. The preferred candidate will also have experience setting up NLP, Machine Learning, AI to assist with automatically tagging content.
  • Minimum of 3 years of healthcare billing in an ambulatory or acute setting is required. Experience is other aspects of healthcare technology will also be considered.

The job title is: Solicitor, Restructuring (ID: 2100013K).Further details:

The DLA Piper team operates across more than 40 countries, but we’re still locally connected. 

Our Restructuring & Insolvency team work on some of the most complex and interesting matters in the market. We partner with a diverse client base that includes debtors, lenders, government entities, trustees, shareholders, senior executives, as well as distressed debt and asset buyers and investors. 

We are currently looking for high performing restructuring solicitor with 5 + years’ experience to join the team based in our Melbourne office

MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

First class lawyers, experience and our unrivalled global coverage are just the beginning of what DLA Piper offers. By joining our team you will have the opportunity to work on a range of matters, advising clients on investigations, enforcement, litigation and asset recovery on a multijurisdictional basis.

As part of our forward thinking team, you will share a client centric approach and take pride in delivering our clients sector focused advice across key expertise areas such as financial services, energy, resources & mining, retail, property and technology.

ABOUT YOU

We know talent is more than what's written on paper. It's the energy you bring and the way you work with your team. 

Your strong communication skills will enable you to develop and maintain high quality relationships with clients.  You will have a mature, confident approach and be highly motivated, thriving in a fast-paced practice. Your organisational skills and ability to manage your own workload, seeking input from team members where needed will support your success.

You will receive first class on the job support and training, working with partners including  Lionel Meehan. You will also have access to our DLA Piper Career Academies, an award-winning international development forum designed to cultivate high performance and support your career goals.

If you're a high performing restructuring lawyer ready to take the next step in your career at a firm that values you, we want to hear from you. Apply now and be part of our future.

ABOUT US

DLA Piper is a global law firm with lawyers located in more than 40 countries throughout the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia Pacific. Our global reach ensures that we can help businesses with their legal needs anywhere in the world. We strive to be the leading global business law firm by delivering quality, service excellence and value to our clients and offering practical and innovative legal solutions to help them succeed. Our clients range from multinational, Global 1000, and Fortune 500 enterprises to emerging companies developing industry-leading technologies, as well as government and public sector bodies.

OUR VALUES

In everything we do connected with our People, our Clients and our Communities, we live by these values:

Be Supportive - we care about others, value diversity and act thoughtfully
Be Collaborative - we give, we share and we join in
Be Bold - we stand tall and challenge ourselves to think big
Be Exceptional - we exceed standards and expectations

DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION

At DLA Piper, diversity and inclusion underpins how we live our values and everything we do.  We believe that everyone has a voice, and that everyone’s voice counts. We know that the rich diversity across our firm makes us stronger, more innovative and creative, which helps us to better serve our clients and communities. We are committed to providing an inclusive working environment and culture across our global firm, where everyone can bring their authentic self to work. 

Diversity of perspective, thought, background and culture combine to make us the leading global law firm; that’s why we actively seek to build balanced teams. We welcome the unique contribution that you will bring to our firm and actively encourage applications from all talented people – however your talent is packaged, whatever your background or circumstance and regardless of how you identify.

We support anyone with a disability or long term health condition to ensure they have the opportunity to perform at their best. If you have not done so already, please let us know if you require any support so we can make the right adjustments and considerations should they be required.

AGILE WORKING

We know that people have responsibilities and interests outside of their career and that as a business, we all benefit from working flexibly. That's why we are open to discussing with candidates the different ways in which we are able to support requests for agile working arrangements.

PRE-ENGAGEMENT SCREENING

In the event that we make an offer to you, and where local legislation permits, we will conduct pre-engagement screening checks that may include but are not limited to your professional and academic qualifications, your eligibility to work in the relevant jurisdiction, any criminal records, your financial stability and references from previous employers.

The job title is: Kaitohutohu Mātāmua Ako/Whanaketanga.Further details: Kia ūkaipō anō te reo Māori:
Koinei te tūrua pō o te rautaki reo Māori hou e kīia nei ko Te Maihi Māori, he mea waihanga e ngāi Māori mā ngā kāinga, ngā hapori me ngā iwi.

I te tīmatanga o te tau 2017 i hui tahi Te Mātāwai me ngā rōpū whai pānga huri noa i te motu ki te kohi haere i ngā kōrero mō ngā kaupapa reo Māori kei ngā kāinga, ngā hapori; ngā wawata kei a rātou e pā ana ki te reo Māori, tae noa ki ngā mahi a Te Mātāwai hei whakatutuki i ēnei wawata. Nā runga i ēnei kohinga kōrero i hua mai ai Maihi Māori 2017-2040.
  
Te tūranga mahi:
Kua ara mai he āheinga pārekareka rawa atu mō tētahi Kaitohutohu Mātāmua Ako/Whanaketanga taiea kia mahi i tēnei wāhi mahi whakahirahira mō tētahi tūranga pūmau tekau mā rua marama te roa. He hunga ngākau nui kei Te Mātāwai e kaha pupuri ana i te mana me te whakarauoratanga o te reo Māori.   
Kei te Kaitohutohu Mātāmua mō ngā take Akoranga/Whanaketanga te haepapa ki te hanga i tētahi pou tarāwaho arataki, whanaketanga, whakangungu hoki mā ngā kaimahi, ngā mema o te Poari me ngā Pae Motuhake. Ko tāu mahi he kōkiri i ētahi hīraunga ako hou kia kairangi ake nei, mā roto i ngā rautaki maha. Āpā noa atu, ko ngā kauhau tuihono ērā, ko ngā papamahi, ko ngā kōwae ako matihiko, me ētahi rauemi hāpai i ngā kaimahi.
Ko tāu mahi he tautohu, he whakaraupapa i ngā hiahia whakangungu, whakawhanake hoki a Te Mātāwai mā te toro ki ngā rōpū whai pānga, tae atu hoki ki te mahi kōtui me ngā pakihi kia mārama ai ngā hiahia ako, ā, he tautohu hoki i ngā wāhi kāore nei e tino kaha ana.

He kōrero mōu ake:
Māu anō koe e kuhu, ā, ka noho mai koe hei kaimahi ako/whanaketanga whai mana i runga i:
  • Te hiranga o ōu pūkenga whakamōhiohio, tō pai ki te kōrero Māori, tō mārama hoki ki ngā tikanga me ngā mātāpono o Te Tiriti o Waitangi;
  • Tētahi huarahi mahi tahi kia pai ai te whakakotahitanga mai o te katoa, kia aro kē mai ētahi atu ki āu ārahitanga;
  • Ōu wheako hirahira mō te ārahi i te whakanaketanga, te hanganga, me te whakatutukitanga o ngā whakangungu arotika, tae noa ki ngā hīraunga ako;
  • Ōu wheako ki te ārahi i te hanganga o ētahi hīraunga ākonga hei whakapakaritanga ake;
  • Ōu mōhio me ōu māramatanga ki ngā mātāpono me ngā ahunga ako.

The job title is: Director, Compliance (SOX).Further details: The Company


This is an excellent opportunity to join a high-profile and reputable industry leader. Due to business expansion, we are currently recruiting for an experienced Director, Compliance with strong experience in SOX compliance.


The Role


Reporting to the Audit Committee and Executive Vice President, you will be responsible for the management and execution of the SOX programme for the group and working closely with the senior management as well as cross functional leaders. The key responsibilities include evaluating design of controls, including acting as a liaison with Business Process Owners (BPOs) on SOX documentation, driving process and control changes to gain controls effectiveness and to improve the control environment. Review the annual SOX scoping, planning materiality and risk assessment and proactively monitor changes that may impact the operating effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting (ICFR). Oversee coordination between internal and external auditors, and BPOs to ensure collaborative execution of the annual evaluation of ICFR. Monitor on a quarterly basis and review the results of control deficiencies identified for management remediation. Oversee the execution of annual walkthroughs of scoped-in business processes and Information Technology General Controls (ITGC) to ensure effective evaluation of the design of ICFR and update all relevant SOX documentation in risk control matrices and flowcharts. Work with BPOs to develop remediation plans for control deficiencies and monitor the remediation status of such plans. Coordinate and assist BPOs with the assessment of adequacy of ICFR of SOC-1 certifications to formally evaluate ICFR at third-party service organizations. Stay informed of changes in legislation, accounting standards and regulatory guidance which impact ICFR, including reviews of PCAOB reports of external auditors. Attend key management committee meetings to stay informed of business changes that may impact the Group's ICFR.


Your Profile


To qualify for this role, you must be a Chartered Accountant/Certified Internal Auditor with a Degree in Accountancy and minimum 15 years of relevant Internal Audit/Compliance experience within Big 4 and commercial firms. It is essential to have a strong background in SOX compliance, assessing the design of controls and executing SOX compliance programs for listed MNCs. Strong knowledge of PCAOB requirements, IFRS and COSO framework will be required. We are looking for a critical thinker with strong leadership and project management capabilities as well as an effective communicator with executive presence.

  • Monitor & report on the investment portfolios that are offered by BNZ

He Waka Eke Noa | Creating Great Together

At BNZ, we're reimagining banking for our customers, helping them be good with money so they can do great things with it. This position sits within our Investment Solutions Team, who are responsible for the risk and return outcomes that our customers experience when investing their money in our funds and/or portfolios.

Te Kaiurungi | About the Role

This is an exciting and challenging opportunity, where you'll support the wider team to ensure that the Managed Investment Schemes (MISs) and Discretionary Investment Management Service (DIMS) portfolios that are offered by BNZ, achieve the best possible investment outcomes for our customers. Key responsibilities include:

  • Regular monitoring of, and reporting on, the MISs and DIMS portfolios that are offered by BNZ
  • Working closely with BNZ's Investment Consultant on the various pieces of work it undertakes for BNZ, such as asset allocation, manager selection
  • Writing and presenting investment recommendations to internal committees and boards
  • Working with the Product, Investment Operations, Investment Communications and Advisory teams to support the management of the existing suite of investment products, and any changes that are made from time to time
  • Keeping up to date with developments in financial markets and the funds management industry
  • Maintaining relationships with the underlying investment managers that have been appointed to BNZ's investment products

Ō Pūkenga | About You

If you have a keen interest in financial markets and investment management, and you're passionate about building your career within our Investment Solutions Team, this is the role for you! You'll have previous experience in a similar role, combined with excellent communication skills. You'll be responsible for condensing and reporting information in a way that is easy to understand to various committees and boards, so attention to detail and exceptional written communication is crucial. We are looking for:

  • Minimum of 3 years' work experience, ideally within a funds management, investment consulting, or financial planning related role or company
  • Business degree, and studying towards the CFA qualification (or already completed)
  • Ability to condense information into a concise summary that is well structured and easy to understand
  • Excellent problem-solving abilities, shows strong initiative and takes a proactive approach to work
  • The ability to self-manage and prioritise their workload to meet deadlines

Nau mai ki te Pēke o Aotearoa | Working at BNZ

At BNZ, we're passionate about building and sustaining a high-performance culture that motivates our people to deliver exceptional results. We know that every BNZer is unique, with a wide range of goals, ambitions, and lifestyles, so we offer a wide range of benefits and working styles to suit you.

  • Wellbeing: Your wellbeing is important to us. When we're at our best, physically and mentally, in and out of work, we can truly create great things together. We're here to support you to be your best with a number of wellbeing initiatives.
  • Leave: We all need a bit of time off every now and then. At BNZ we're proud to offer the generous leave options you need and deserve - whether it's for a special occasion, an unexpected event, or an extended vacation.
  • Flexibility: We're big on helping you balance life and work. We offer a range of flexible working options that help you be your best, wherever you're based. Talk to us about how we can make this work for you.

Haere mai ki Te Peke o Aotearoa | Come to the Bank of New Zealand

Inspired by your customers and energised through success, BNZ has the environment and opportunities for you to contribute to a high achieving New Zealand. Come join us and let's create great together.

Please submit a cover letter and CV by end of Tuesday 23rd November 2021.  

If you would like to know more about Life at BNZ and how you can help re imagine banking for our customers, please visit www.bnzcareers.co.nz or click the ‘apply now’ button to submit your confidential application.

Job Purpose

You will be joining the Student Life Office to support the NUS School of Computing's (SoC) student community to build a vibrant campus life while encouraging wellness, well-being, and welfare to make each student's experience in university as productive and meaningful as possible.

Job Description

Student Support and Case Management

  • Provide a friendly and safe environment for students to voice their concerns, involving close family members if necessary, and seek support at faculties with minimal stigma.
  • Provide first-line support and assessment of students and refer medium- to high-risk cases to the University Counselling Services (UCS).
  • Monitor & reach out to existing cases of at-risk students and students who are referred by UCS.
  • Offer individual consultation and/or pastoral care to students and referring them to the correct offices in NUS (e.g. Office of Financial Aid (OFA), University Health Centre (UHC), UCS, Office of Housing Services(OHS), NUS Care Unit (NCU), etc. based on their needs and concerns).
  • Work with faculty staff to handle at risk students and contact students who have been missing classes.
  • Advise and advocate for students who need support for Leave of Absence, special considerations for exam or assignments.
  • Manage students on Stay Home Notice/Quarantine Order regarding their wellbeing and related academic request and queries.
  • Manage cases on violation of non-academic offence and provide care and support to students.
  • Manage cases on No-Contact Order (NCO).

Peer Student Support at SoC

  • Assist in the setting up of PitStop@SoC.
  • Assist in development of Peer Student Support Group (PSSG) at SoC Training and Outreach.
  • Organise mental health literacy programmes for SoC staff and students.
  • Organize mental wellness programmes for students customised to the faculty's needs and context to encourage support for self-care and stress management.

Student and Alumni Engagement

  • Engage the student community and student groups through active participation in faculty events.
  • Reach out to international students to provide assistance and support in settling into NUS/Singapore.
  • Organise activities to encourage integration between local and international students such as workshops on cross-cultural sensitivity/awareness.
  • Development and management of mentorship programmes for SoC (senior-junior and alumni-student).
Job Requirement
  • A recognized University degree in psychology, social work or equivalent.
  • At least 2 years of experience in providing guidance and general wellness support to youths and young adults, including appropriate management of students in crisis.
  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills.
  • Excellent listening skills.
  • Ability to prioritize.
  • Able to work in a team and adept at managing multiple priorities effectively.
  • Resourceful with good organisational, planning and project management skills.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications.
  • Familiarity with student affairs in higher education.
  • High proficiency in Mandarin to be able to communicate with next-of-kin of international students fromChina.
  • Ability to create infographics.
  • Versatile with social media.
Covid-19 Message

At NUS, the health and safety of our staff and students are one of our utmost priorities, and COVID-vaccination supports our commitment to ensure the safety of our community and to make NUS as safe and welcoming as possible. Many of our roles require a significant amount of physical interactions with students/staff/public members. In accordance with Singapore's legal requirements, unvaccinated workers will not be able to work on the NUS premises with effect from 15 January 2022. As such, job applicants will need to be fully COVID-19 vaccinated to secure successful employment with NUS.

The job title is: Research Assistant (CML).Further details:
Job Description

The Centre for Maritime Law (CML) at the Faculty of Law, National University of Singapore, was launched on 3 September 2015 and focuses broadly on international trade, transport and shipping law-related issues. It undertakes research and hosts events of scholarly value to academics, professionals, and government institutions. Its objective is to enhance the development of commercial maritime law in Singapore, the region, and further afield. CML's continuing achievements include a highly-regarded Working Paper Series (WPS), available at https://law.nus.edu.sg/cml/publications/ [link removed], and the CML CMI Database, Judicial Decisions on International Conventions, available at https://cmlcmidatabase.org/. [link removed]

The Director of CML is Professor Stephen Girvin, MPA Professor of Maritime Law, and the Deputy Director is Associate Professor Paul Myburgh.

CML is inviting applications from suitable candidate(s), who are at the beginning of their professional careers, to conduct research and participate in CML's work. Depending on qualifications, background and expertise, the successful applicant(s) will be appointed as a Research Assistant in CML.

The successful applicant will join CML's existing full-time and Adjunct research staff (see https://law.nus.edu.sg/cml/personnel/ [link removed]).

Benefits

The position(s) will carry the following benefits:

1. Employment on a full-time contract at NUS Law for one year and, subject to satisfactory performance, may be renewable for a second year.

2. A remuneration package, commensurate with qualifications and experience.

3. Allocation of designated workspace within CML.

Duties

The duties associated with the position(s) are as follows:

1. The successful applicant will be expected to be in residence throughout the term of his or her appointment, subject to the normal NUS terms as to annual leave.

2. Depending on experience, the successful applicant will be expected to develop his or her own research agenda, including undertaking research projects on maritime law, leading to publication in English-language refereed journals, during his or her term of appointment. The proposed research agenda MUST also include writing working papers for publication in the CML Working Paper Series (https://law.nus.edu.sg/cml/publications/ [link removed]).

3. The successful applicant will also be required to present his or her research and to participate in and contribute to CML seminars.

4. The successful applicant is expected to assist in CML's research projects and initiatives, including the CML CMI Database, Judicial Decisions on International Conventions (https://www.cmlcmidatabase.org/).

5. The successful applicant may be asked to act as research assistant to the Director or Deputy Director of CML, as assigned by the Director of CML.

Qualifications

Requirements

The selection committee will consider the following criteria in making an appointment for the position of Research Assistant in CML:

1. The successful applicant will be of exceptional calibre.

2. For appointment as a Research Assistant, the successful applicant must have an Honours degree (or equivalent) in law, preferably with a postgraduate degree in maritime law (or an interest in pursuing such a degree), or demonstrate a strong interest in maritime law.

3. Applications are invited from those with interests in any branch of commercial maritime or shipping law or admiralty law or marine insurance law, including the international sale of goods carried by sea, maritime conflict of laws, maritime dispute resolution (including maritime arbitration, especially in the Asian context), and offshore oil and gas law. A demonstrated interest in contemporary research on maritime law, such as the impact of COVID-19 on the maritime sector, ship finance in the 21st century, and decarbonisation and the shipping industry, may be an advantage.

4. Applications are not sought from those with primary interests in the international law of the sea, ocean law and policy, or international environmental law.

Application procedure


Interested applicants are invited to apply and submit their applications directly at our NUS Career Portal. These must comprise:


1. Covering letter

This should explain the reason for your interest in the position and address your ability to perform the duties listed above.


2. Application Form

The application form should be completed and submitted together with the other required documents. Applicants may download the:

- Application form HERE [link removed]


3. Curriculum Vitae

A detailed curriculum vita should be submitted containing complete and detailed information on academic institutions, honours, awards, all publications to date, and all professional experience (current and previous, including dates of employment and job descriptions).


4. Letters of Recommendation

The application must be supported by two references from academic referees. Applicants must arrange for their referees to send their references to the address below by the closing date.


5. Submission of Application Materials

Interested applicants are invited to apply and submit their applications directly at our NUS Career Portal.


6. Closing Date

The closing date for the receipt of applications and references is Wednesday, 24 November 2021. Late applications cannot be considered.


7. Shortlisting and Interview

Shortlisted applicants should expect to be interviewed, via Zoom, during late November to early December 2021. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted concerning the status of their application.

More Information

求職資訊
參閱在求職及面試時須注意的事項。如須撰寫求職信及履歷表，可參考
求職信及履歷表範本

在接受聘用前，你應清楚知道僱主的身份，詳情可參閱「保存僱傭紀錄---僱員參考手冊」。

求職人士請注意：
  • 空缺咭展示的職位空缺資料，包括職位名稱、職責內容、工作時間、薪金等，均是由僱主提供。如果求職人士在面試時，僱主提出不合理的要求，或所提供的僱傭條件與本處登記的資料不符，請盡快通知本處。為免墮入求職陷阱，在面試時應注意聘用條件（包括計薪方法、工資期、休息日安排等），了解職位的工作範圍及入職要求，並留意工作環境。此外，請特別留意工作性質及內容會否抵觸現行法例，切勿因急於求職而接受聘用從事非法工作。
  • 僱主及職業介紹所向本處遞交職位招聘表時，已承諾會按照《最低工資條例》的規定，就任何工資期，支付不少於法定最低工資水平的工資予受聘有關職位並受《最低工資條例》涵蓋的人士 。
  • 如你有合理懷疑僱主未有遵守《僱傭條例》、《僱員補償條例》、《最低工資條例》，可致電熱線2717 1771（由1823接聽）或電郵至enquiry@labour.gov.hk 查詢。至於涉及《性別歧視條例》、《殘疾歧視條例》、《家庭崗位歧視條例》或《種族歧視條例》的查詢，請聯絡平等機會委員會。
  • 根據《最低工資條例》的規定，僱主須就任何工資期，確保支付僱員不少於按下列方法計算的最低工資：

    最低工資=僱員於工資期的總工作時數 x 法定最低工資水平（即每小時40元1）
    1由2023年5月1日起，法定最低工資水平已調升至每小時40元。

    • 如就工資期須支付予僱員的工資少於最低工資，僱員有權就該工資期獲付這差額（即「額外報酬」）。該僱員的僱傭合約須視為他有權就該工資期獲得額外報酬，而該額外報酬亦適用於計算根據其他相關法例所應獲得的款項。
    • 有關法定最低工資的定義及計算詳情，請瀏覽 《法定最低工資：僱主及僱員參考指引》或致電 24 小時查詢熱線 2717 1771（由「1823」接聽）。

The job title is: High Care Support Worker - Munster.Further details: Permanent Part Time - Providing specialized support in Munster
  • Hourly rate starting at $32.21 during training plus penalties
  • Paid km's & time travelled between supports - work in your local community
  • Ongoing training and development opportunities

We are looking for professional support workers to be a part of a family orientated, supportive and dedicated team, providing person centered care to an active Ventilated Quadriplegic man.

Located in the Lake Coogee area this position requires 24/7-hour supports, 365 days of the year working in a 2:1 and 3:1 work environment with crossover staff. The purpose-built house is well organised and support workers are guided by a team of allied health professionals including an on call GP and clinical registered nurses.

Our customer requires various supports but what we are looking for is to fill these supports throughout the week - Monday-Sunday : 6am-1pm, 11am-9.30pm and 9pm-6am (active overnight awake shift).

There's no 'typical day' but it may include....

  • Administering medication (training provided)
  • A range of clinical care & skills required - bowel and catheter care, ventilator/oxygen management, Tracheostomy care (training provided)
  • Manual handling (training provided by OT & Physio)
  • Providing reliable, timely and flexible services that best meet the needs of the individual and their family
  • Problem solving issues with the person and/or their family, and the team
  • Regular communication and engagement with your local team 

It can be tricky at times. So a positive attitude, compassion and resilience is a must have and, if it does get tough, the team will have your back!

We're looking for:

  • Previous support work experience (desirable)
  • Prior experience in clinical work (desirable)
  • Reliability, flexibility and a positive attitude
  • Demonstrated communication skills and a can-do attitude to help ensure our customers receive flexible and individualised support
  • Ability to problem solve, think creatively and find innovative solutions

You'll receive:

  • An hourly rate of $32.21 plus super whilst training; increasing to $34.23 plus super once deemed competent by a Nurse Consultant
  • Increase your take-home pay with the option to salary package up to $18,550
  • Opportunity to gain a nationally recognised Certificate III or Certificate IV in Individual Support
  • Get up to 8% Discount on Health Cover with HBF
  • A mobile phone for work use
  • Access to Employee Assistance Program -independent confidential counselling service
  • A supportive and inclusive team environment
  • Great work-life balance!

What we need from you:

  • A current First Aid certificate & Working with Children's Check or willingness to obtain one (the successful candidate can obtain through Avivo)
  • A valid driver's licence and a reliable vehicle (essential)
  • Making an appointment to this position is subject to a satisfactory NDIS Worker Screening Check
  • Avivo encourages applicants to be fully vaccinated against covid-19 including the seasonal flu vaccination.


To apply, attach your updated resume.

If you are shortlisted for an interview, we will notify you via email or by phone.

Closing Date Thursday 6th July 2023

Avivo values a diverse workforce with different life experiences, skills and backgrounds including people with disability, First Nations Peoples, LGBTQIA+ and people from all culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds. We encourage you to apply.

Role Title: Relief Caretaker - Maitai Catchment Reserve
Location: Nelson
Contract Type: Casual (hours vary)

The Opportunity
We are looking for a multiskilled Relief Caretaker for the Maitai Catchment Reserve. This is a casual role to provide cover for weekends, annual leave, and absences of the acting Caretaker Couple. The successful candidate will need to temporarily live on site (24/7 operation) while working, accommodation is provided.

This is a great opportunity for someone with flexible time on their hands, who enjoys the outdoors , has practical skills, can operate tools and machinery, and is good at problem solving.

The key responsibilities are:

  • To operate the Maitai Catchment Reserve in a manner that ensures water of the required standard is available for supply in the most efficient, timely and safe manner and ensure that the surrounds are maintained in a safe condition for staff, client, visitors, and the public.
  • Operate tools, vehicles, and equipment, including general maintenance to best practice on request
  • Collect water samples and report test results.
  • Collect and maintain information necessary for reporting to the client.
  • Ensure all work is carried out in compliance with the relevant job and work instruction.
  • Understand and embrace our Living Safely approach.
  • Operate and maintain the Maitai Catchment Reserve and associated infrastructure on request

What you'll bring to the table
To successfully undertake the duties associated with this assignment you will have a knowledge and understanding of trade and maintenance, enjoy a multitude of tasks and be able to respond to enquiries and urgent needs calmly and professionally.

  • Full class 1 license; 4x4 experience is advantageous
  • Confident with various property/reserve maintenance tasks (i. e. fencing, tractor driving, operating chainsaws/tools)
  • Comfortable to stay in a semi-remote location (weekends or longer to cover annual leave)
  • Ability to manage livestock on site
  • Manage expectations from various parties to run the operation of the reserve while the Caretaker is on leave
  • Have an unwavering commitment towards living safely with a safety record to match
  • Excellent communication skills, proficient computer skills (to produce reports)
  • Be a reliable individual with a strong work ethic

Who we are
You've probably seen us around - we build and maintain infrastructure that improves the quality of life across New Zealand and Australia. Everything, from roads and bridges, to energy, water and communication. We're big and growing but this will always be a family business.

Here at Fulton Hogan, we don't just talk about our REAL Values, we live them too. Our people are the most important part of our business and we're always looking for people who are passionate about the work they do. If that's you, we'd like to invite you to become part of our family and join us in our commitment to ensuring the Good Work we do will make a positive difference.

Sound like you?
If you are looking for a role to showcase your skills, build a long-lasting legacy, and want to help us build on our Good Work culture, then we want to hear from you.

All successful candidates must under-go and pass a pre-employment medical and drug & alcohol screen.

.Country Codes: NZ.Salary information: nan.

The job title is: Palliative Care Bereavement Counsellor/Coordinator.Further details:

This position qualifies for a Recruitment Incentive Package up to the value of $5,000 under the NSW Health Rural Health Workforce Incentive Scheme.

This scheme recognises the role key health workers play in enabling the delivery of rural and remote health services, and aims to provide incentives over and above award entitlements, to attract and retain staff in these areas.

For more information, please discuss incentive options with the contact person for this role

Employment Type: Permanent Full Time
Position Classification: Social Worker Level 3
Remuneration: $105093 - $108612 + Super
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: REQ371122
Location: Broken Hill NSW

What you'll be doing

  • The Bereavement Counsellor/Coordinator is responsible for coordination of the Bereavement Service within the Broken Hill Specialist Palliative Care Service which includes the delivery of specialist bereavement counselling, support and follow up to family members and carers of deceased patients known to Broken Hill Palliative Care Service, and if required, the Dareton Palliative Care Service for complex bereavement. Using education, training and mentoring the role will build the capacity of the multidisciplinary team to support bereaved people known to FWLHD Palliative Care Services.
  • Develop bereavement resources for the FWLHD Palliative Care Services.

 

Incentives

  • 5 weeks paid annual leave per year
  • Salary packaging (pay less tax!)
  • Paid Allocated Day Off (ADO) Every Month
  • Isolation & climate allowance
  • Remote Area Housing Assistance Benefits
  • Special rates at local gyms
  • Employee Meal & Entertainment Card
  • A comfortable country lifestyle that supports balance & wellbeing

About Broken Hill

A true “Oasis in the Outback”, Broken Hill is a thriving regional town in far west NSW full of diversity, history and character. Being Australia’s first city to be Nationally Heritage Listed, Broken Hill is a culturally rich town with a vibrant art scene with over 20 galleries! The unique attractions, festivals and beautiful natural landscapes see tourists flock from all over, but the ones who stay quickly fall in love with the place and its liveability.

With a population just shy of 20,000, Broken Hill is small enough to allow for a relaxed country lifestyle, while big enough to provide all the desired facilities of a regional hub including major supermarkets and retail stores, excellent schools (7 primary & 2 high), multiple gyms & aquatic centre, well-known fast food franchises and a plethora of trendy restaurants, pubs and cafés.

The beautiful Murray-Riverina region is just 2.5 hours from Broken Hill, and after a short, 5-hour drive you can enjoy the beautiful Barossa Valley – South Australia’s internationally acclaimed wine region. For a town so unique, it’s really not that far away with just a short 1hr15m flight from Adelaide, a 2hr flight from Melbourne or a 2hr 30m flight from Sydney.

Broken Hill truly is a town like no other with a supportive community that will welcome you with open arms. We can’t wait to see you soon!


Selection Criteria

  1. Clinical Psychologist with full registration with the Psychologists Registration Board of NSW or Social Worker eligible for membership of the Australian Association of Social Workers.
  2. Experience as a counselling clinician in bereavement, palliative care or end of life contexts and specialist knowledge of bereavement, loss and grief processes. Post-graduate tertiary qualifications related to counselling desirable.
  3. Proven ability to work independently, manage service coordination and complex cases effectively.
  4. Demonstrated ability to provide education and training to health professionals in the areas of grief, loss and bereavement and clinical supervision.
  5. Demonstrated ability to work effectively as a member of a multidisciplinary team, which may include participation in quality improvement, evaluation or research.
  6. Demonstrated high level verbal and written communication, negotiation, liaison, advocacy and conflict resolution skills as well as high level computer and data entry skills
  7. Demonstrated ability to participate in organisational and service planning, development and quality improvement
  8. Current driver licence and willingness to travel throughout LHD.

About the Far West LHD

The Far West Local Health District is the westernmost LHD under NSW Health, providing high quality public health services to the communities in far west NSW. Our vision is to create "excellence in rural and remote healthcare". The key to our success is our diverse and inclusive workforce. We employ over 800 clinicians and support staff across 9 health facilities in Broken Hill, Balranald, Dareton, Ivanhoe, Menindee, Tibooburra, Wentworth, White Cliffs and Wilcannia. We encourage you to consider joining our friendly team for a meaningful and rewarding career in rural and remote healthcare.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Australian-owned, Award-winning, and ASX listed, Viva Leisure are Australia’s second-largest and fastest-growing operator of health and fitness experiences and facilities. Viva Leisure operates in all segments of health and fitness and our range of offerings includes big-box health clubs, express gyms, high-intensity group training studios, pilates, yoga, aquatics, women's only facilities, personal training and more.

Viva Leisure, parent company to Club Lime is looking for those interested in future development opportunities which may lead to club management, as part of our Future Leaders Programme. This programme is designed to develop Assistant Club Managers into future Club Managers and provide a pathway to manage your very own club.

Founded in 2004, some of our key brands are Club Lime, Hiit Republic, Plus Fitness, GroundUp and Rebalance. We currently have a footprint of over 300 facilities across Australia and internationally, including both corporate owned and franchised sites. Our head offices are in Canberra ACT and Sydney NSW.

Viva Leisure have the mission of connecting health and wellness to as many people as possible through our range of awesome, affordable and accessible facilities.  Our vision is to be the #1 in the industry for our employees, our shareholders, our franchisees, our communities, and of course our members.

This expression of interest provides the opportunity for all looking to grow and develop into leaders across our selected Club Lime venues. These opportunities allow you to learn from our leadership team within the space and undertake upskilling, exceptional personalised development, and a positive platform for constructive feedback filled with growth and passion.  

You will be responsible for providing exceptional leadership, management, and passion for health and well-being to all members and employees associated with Club Lime. You will have the opportunity to learn from experienced leaders in the fitness industry, gain exposure to different areas of the business and develop the skills and knowledge to become a successful Club Manager. Day-to-day duties could consist of servicing clubs, maximising sales memberships, supporting members with general queries, club tours for prospective members, and ensuring that the club environment is clean and well-presented for all.

 Skills & Experience

CLUB LIME

We are excited to share with you this opportunity which allows fulfilling and rewarding experiences. First and foremost, our clubs are dedicated to creating a positive and supportive environment for our members and employees. The job title is: Senior Urban Designer.Further details:

Me Heke Ki Pōneke - Wellington City Council has declared an ecological and climate emergency as it adopts a blueprint for becoming a zero-carbon city - Our City Tomorrow. It's an exciting time to join our team of city shapers and play a key role in transforming how people live, work, play and travel across the city!

Kia mahi ngātahi mō Pōneke mō tōna āpōpō Working together for Wellington's future.

People love living in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington. We are a vibrant, connected, and compact city that frequently tops global city quality-of-life surveys. So, it's no wonder more people want to live here. By 2050 we're expecting 50,0000 to 80,000 more Wellingtonians, and 25% more people coming into the central city each workday from across the region.

To ensure our city continues to thrive as a healthy, safe and sustainable creative capital, where people live, work and play, we have committed to delivering an ambitious, exciting Long-term Plan. This Plan includes a number of key strategies that put people and innovation at the heart of how we design and deliver a more creative, prosperous, and greener capital. Our Planning and Environment group is leading many of these strategies, from delivering more affordable housing, installing new bike networks, to helping our capital become a net zero-carbon city by 2050.

This role sits within the Urban Regeneration and Design team (within the City Design unit in the Planning & Environment Group) that will work across the City Design unit, the organisation and in collaboration with the community and private sector to embrace initiative to influence positive city outcomes in private development.

The Senior Urban Designer will contribute to the Design Review workstream (the gateway to all public and private developments), champion a 'design led' approach, and undertake timely urban design assessment, technical review and evaluation of development proposals. Additionally, this role involves a unique opportunity to contribute to establishing a Design Review Programme and associated Design Review Panels. The role's contributions to various aspects of the Design Review Team interrelate to help ensure that Wellington's future growth meets the ambitious goals of Our City Tomorrow, and that all new development (whether public or private) is held to best-practice urban design standards.

Although detailed knowledge of the Resource Management Act (RMA) is not necessary, the successful applicant should understand how the District Plan assists Council in achieving the best practice urban design outcomes and sustainable management goals. Our ideal person will have a relevant degree in urban design related field such as landscape architecture, architecture, planning or related. 5+ years of experience in architectural practices or other relevant construction industries would be an advantage.

This is a collaborative role which involves close working relationships with a diverse group of stakeholders especially in a complex political environment, with your strong influencing skills, you will be able to get alongside the stakeholders, understand their imperatives, and look for the win-win. You will be calm headed and resilient with the ability to listen, empathise and form awesome relationships in a high-pressure environment.

More importantly you will be an awesome team player who gets excited about the public life of cities and committed to making a difference by creating Wellington as an Urban Village with a Wild Edge. Council values and celebrates the uniquely compact and vibrant qualities of Wellington and is committed to best practice built and natural environment outcomes. Naturally we think our council is the best - we offer range of benefits that includes flexible working model, 5 weeks annual leave after 2 years of continuous service for permanent staff and much more!

If this opportunity excites you, then we would welcome your application!

All applications for this role must be submitted online and will be treated in strict confidence. If you would like more information or have a confidential chat before applying, you are welcome to contact Farzad Zamani, Manager Urban Regeneration & Design at farzad.zamani@wcc.govt.nz. Applicants must be legally eligible to work in New Zealand or must be in the process of obtaining a visa with a set date to come to NZ.

Applications will close 10 April 2022.

At Wellington City Council, we have a responsibility to safeguard the community we serve, while also keeping our team, whānau and friends, and other external parties safe.

Our COVID-19 Vaccination Policy applies to Wellington City Council employees who are either covered by the requirements of a Public Health Order or whose roles are deemed to require vaccination, as a result of the risk assessment process, for health and safety purposes, or because they are working in a site using a COVID-19 Vaccination Pass (CVP).

Our Vaccination Policy covers this role, which means COVID-19 vaccinations are mandatory.

If successful, it will be a requirement of your employment that you are fully vaccinated, and that you provide your personal vaccine pass as an official record of your COVID-19 vaccination status.

The job title is: Project Manager.Further details:

Centre for Innovation in Healthcare (CIH), National University Health System
Project Manager


Background

The Center for Innovation in Healthcare (CIH), is a one-stop hub with the goal of facilitating clinical adoption of practice changing innovations for public good and global impact. CIH achieves this goal by complementing other partners in the innovation ecosystem.

By virtue of CIH being part of National University Health System, CIH focuses on clinical testing and health technology assessment by leveraging its core assets of patients, healthcare professionals, and health data.

The Project Manager will run exciting innovation projects at various stages of the healthcare innovation journey, to progress them towards the final goal of deployment and clinical adoption of the innovation. You will also be the first point of contact to manage new interest to engage CIH services and also lead initiatives and events to support CIH's goal.

You will work closely with a diverse team comprising project managers, clinical research coordinators (CRC) and business managers to provide the support for our healthcare innovators to achieve CIH's goal.

Join us if you have a passion for healthcare innovations!

Duties and Responsibilities:
1. Manages communications for new interests including requests from student innovators, clinician innovators and healthcare startups, to engage CIH
2. Works closely with CIH team to screen external and internal innovators interested to conduct usability trial studies, clinical trials or Health Technology Assessments (HTA) in NUHS entities
3. Lead the end-to-end project management with CIH CRCs to ensure the smooth running of the projects once accepted
4. Works closely with CIH CRCs and CIH administration manager to assist investigators in preparing the study protocol and all relevant documents in compliance with hospital policies, regulatory and ethical requirements
5. Facilitates development of innovation projects by seeking funding and facilitating negotiations to ensure that the interests of NUHS are advanced
6. Engages appropriate stakeholders, advisors and partners to provide advice or support to advance the projects
7. Works closely with the CIH Business Manager to strategise the use of the innovation displays in CIH Showroom to advance CIH goal
8. Assist in forging of new partnerships or maintain relationships with CIH partners to support CIH innovators
9. Work closely with CIH team to coordinate CIH events or carry out new initiatives to support CIH innovators and partners
10. Any other duties that are assigned by the Reporting Officer

Job specification:
- At least Bachelor of Science. Other qualifications in Business or Entrepreneurship preferred.
- 3-5 years of relevant experience in Innovation Activities including (1) Facilitating innovation collaborations (2) Licensing / Commercialisation activities (3) Project Management.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
- A strong team player
- Have keen interest in medical technology innovations
- Good to be familiar with Human Biomedical Research Act (HBRA) and Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)
- Able to work in a complex organisational environment, with a need to balance expectations of multiple stakeholders
- Possess strong analytical skills
- Able to tackle complicated research, regulatory and contractual issues independently
- Proficient in I.T. systems and MS Office applications

When working in a respite service you would support wellbeing by providing a listening ear, supporting on site activities such as mindfulness, medication, maintaining a large home, cooking, cleaning and hosting visiting clinical teams.

Some health and disability sector employers may require workers to be vaccinated. This is because workers come into close contact with people likely to get seriously ill if they get COVID-19. Having undertaken a thorough health and safety analysis with regards to Covid-19, we have determined that vaccination is required for our workforce (two primary doses and at least one booster).

The job title is: Senior physiotherapist - private practice - award winning clinic.Further details:

Salary - $90000-$130000 package based on experience

About you

Currently we have had a senior fulltime physio with a busy caseload resign who is moving away from the area, and this opportunity is for ideally an immediate start but for the ideal candidate a start between now and January 2024. You would be stepping into her busy caseload and not having to build a caseload from scratch which means you have the opportunity to hit commission bonuses from the very beginning which is rare when starting a new role.

We are seeking physiotherapists who:

  • Have experience working in a busy private practice
  • Live in or willing to relocate to the beautiful Redcliffe Peninsula and North Brisbane region
  • Are strongly committed to excellence in private practice and love private practice
  • Enjoy being in a busy, stimulating clinic environment
  • Value working alongside a high performing team
  • Want to harness the learning opportunities that working in an experienced team provides
  • Desire personal growth and mentoring from our leadership team
  • Are seeking something more from the next step of your career through our industry first pathways
  • May be frustrated about the lack of career progression in your current career
  • May feel that the “mentoring” you had been promised in your current role hasn’t materialised
  • Want to learn from an owner who is one of Australia’s most recognised physiotherapy private practice leaders
  • Are truly team players and have demonstrated abilities when it comes to being part of a team
  • Ideally you have a special area of interest within private practice - we currently have physios with special expertise in clinical pilates, pelvic health, gym based rehab, and occupational health
  • The physio leaving is a general musc physio and we are ideally looking for a like for like replacement
  • In your current role due to COVID related challenges you may not have a busy enough caseload to generate the income you desire - and this is something we can provide for you

The role

  • The hours required for this role are completely negotiable - anywhere from 15 hours to 38 hours a week is fine for the right applicant (although our ideal applicant is wanting fulltime or close to fulltime employment)
  • You will be replacing an existing fulltime therapist with a busy caseload that you will step straight into and not have to build up
  • You will treat a mix of private musculoskeletal clients and we will assist you in building a niched caseload to suit a special area of interest
  • Appointment lengths will be customised to your needs (both initial and follow up consultations) and level of experience
  • We will consider applicants with any level of experience, although our preferred candidates will have 5+ years in private practice
  • Your level of experience will determine your salary package, and our existing therapists’ salary packages range from a base award salary to upwards of $50 an hour
  • Annual salary package will range from $90000 to $130000 pro rata including your base salary plus all bonuses and entitlements (based on experience and qualifications)
  • Your salary package includes a bonus/commission structure which allows you to take home an extra $20000-$30000 per year in performance based bonuses
  • You will have access to a PD budget, internal formal and informal clinic mentoring, world class external paid mentors the clinic engages, and the clinic hosts 1-2 onsite physiotherapy professional development courses a year which you attend for free (COVID permitting)
  • Our clinical mentor is highly skilled 23 year experienced private practice physiotherapist who will mentor you on a weekly basis
  • We have a highly skilled admin team including a dedicate off desk Practice Manager to assist you at all levels of your role, especially with client retention
  • Each quarter we close the clinic for a team day focused on helping you grow personally and set goals that are meaningful to you

About the clinic

Scarborough Physio and Health is a multi award winning boutique clinic with a bustling team of 20 opposite beautiful Scarborough Beach on the Redcliffe Peninsula. We have grown through COVID and weathered the challenges of the last couple of years and have come out the other side. We are a strong business with a 20 year history and an exceptionally large and diverse client base.

Our vision is to make Redcliffe the healthiest and best place to live in Australia through positively influencing the lives of every person on the Redcliffe Peninsula. We have so far helped more than 20000 people (1 in 3 people in our region) with pain and injury and that number is growing rapidly.

Comprising a team of 5 physios, remedial massage therapy, pilates and clinical psychology we service clients with complex needs who form strong bonds with their therapists over long periods of time and require expert care and high levels of customer service and collaborative treatment.

With a dedicated leadership team including a clinic owner with a negligible caseload and a dedicated practice manager who is off the front desk you have a management team who is dedicated to your success and is available for intensive induction, mentoring and coaching at every stage of your journey.

Our induction programme is industry best and guaranteed you success in your role with a 6-12 month and ongoing training programme.

We have formal and informal clinical and non clinical mentoring and you will have a mentor, buddy and leader assigned to you.

Boasting an industry first 5 step career pathway that can lead to profit share, leadership and management, specialisation, high income or lifestyle our goal is for our physios to earn 6 figures and work no more than 4 days per week.

Be treated with the professionalism of a corporate environment without losing the small town feel of a family owned and operated business.

Our clinicians most love the customised caseload and ability to treat their favourite types of clients, the warm and friendly and beautiful environment with a purpose built rehab gym, the dedicated leadership team to assist with their growth, development and challenges, the mentoring pathways to help them achieve excellence, and the salary package to value their expertise and help them achieve their personal goals - buying houses, overseas holidays, flexible working hours and other perks (including a state of the art coffee machine!).

We utilise the latest practice management software and technology to make your job easier and rewarding but also to aid you in taking your performance to the next level and we have invested heavily in our systems and technology this last 12 months with the goal of making our team members' work lives easier and better.

What next?

We welcome the opportunity to meet you and lead you through a professional process to not only determine your fit for Scarborough Physio and Health, but also whether we are the right clinic for you and the next stage in your private practice physiotherapy career.

For candidates located outside Queensland we are open to assisting you with relocation expenses for the right person.

For suitably qualified applicants outside Australia we are an employer registered to sponsor international physiotherapists, but your physiotherapy degree must be equivalent to an Australian physiotherapy undergraduate qualification., and your skills, communication and command of the English language must be at an exceptional standard to be considered for this role.

Applicants without AHPRA registration will not be considered for this role.

Preference will be given to those who apply for this role as soon as possible, and we will interview you as soon as your application comes through - so apply ASAP to give yourself the best chance to secure what could be your dream job!

The job title is: Principal Advisors - Renewable Energy Projects.Further details:

Principal Advisors, Renewable Energy Projects

  • Excellent opportunity to join the Renewable Energy Projects team
  • Hub based location, Perth, Brisbane, or Montreal
  • Core new Renewable positions where your expertise can shine

Rio Tinto has recently launched a dedicated team to deliver large renewable energy solutions across our major jurisdictions. Rio Tinto Energy Development is focusing on accelerating the development of future energy assets and securing high quality renewable energy development optionality. The team's focus on the provision of green energy will enable the decarbonisation of the company’s existing industrial operations and support Rio Tinto’s future growth

About the role

RTED has been established to support and accelerate the delivery of the Rio Tinto strategy. RTED is will drive project delivery, with multiple renewable energy workstreams moving at pace. To advance Rio Tinto’s decarbonisation agenda, RTED will work closely with existing teams across our Product Groups and supporting functions to accelerate the delivery of renewables into the energy supply mix.

RTED includes a centralised Renewable Energy Projects team that will work with the assets outside of our core energy regions where we see renewable energy as both an abatement lever and a future growth function moving forward (Quebec, Pacific and the Pilbara). These assets outside of the core regions have detailed and complicated renewable energy solutions ahead of them and include both existing and new growth assets. The team is dedicated to supporting renewable abatement outcomes and will support the Product Groups to drive action to enable faster adoption and execution of renewable energy solutions. Importantly, the team is more than a consulting service, and will stand alongside the Product Groups when decisions are made on renewable opportunities. To strengthen this, we are looking for Principal Advisors in the Renewable Energy Projects Team. These key positions can be based in Perth, Brisbane, or Montreal.

The candidates we are looking to appoint will have recent and credible experience with renewable project delivery, renewable energy deal creation and/or renewable energy construction. You will work alongside existing site teams, bringing deep expertise to external negotiations, or development of in-house renewable assets, and will leverage your understanding on renewable penetration limits.

You will get to partner with the business on options analysis (quantitative and qualitative) and demonstrate your execution capability to support project delivery and long-term optionality.

With your influencing, interpersonal and relationship skills, your analysis and presentations will be integral in creating commercially focussed solutions and communicating effectively with senior stakeholders. Your role will play a key part in delivering best-in-class renewable outcomes across our assets and creating a winning culture to make a difference.

The intention of these roles is to deliver alongside the Product Groups, and the successful applicant will prepare and carry discussions with the wider group about abatement opportunities.

This is an excellent time to join the business in key roles, set the agenda and deliver results. People who can think, act and achieve, whilst driving change, providing direction and delivering to business needs will be able to start here and go anywhere.

We have opportunities for both Principal Commercial Advisors and Principal Technical Advisors

What we offer

Be recognised for your contribution, your thinking and your hard work, and go home knowing you’ve helped the world progress.

  • A work environment where safety is always the number one priority
  • A culture to support flexible working options
  • A permanent position working directly for Rio Tinto
  • A competitive base salary reflective of your skills and experience with annual incentive program
  • Comprehensive medical benefits including subsidised private health insurance for employees and immediate family
  • Attractive share ownership plan
  • Company provided insurance cover
  • Extensive salary sacrifice & salary packaging options
  • Career development & education assistance to further your technical or leadership ambitions
  • Ongoing access to family-friendly health and medical wellbeing support
  • Leave for all of life’s reasons (vacation/annual, paid parental, sick leave)
  • Exclusive employee discounts (banking, accommodation, cars, retail and more)
  • Possible domestic relocation assistance

Every Voice Matters

At Rio Tinto, we particularly welcome and encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, women, the LGBTI+ community, mature workers, people with disabilities and people from different cultural backgrounds.

We are committed to an inclusive environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are essential to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation or anything else that makes us different.

Applications for this role will close on December19th 2021 however we do reserve the right to close the role earlier.


Conseillers Principaux, Projets d'énergie renouvelable

  • Excellente opportunité de rejoindre l'équipe des Projets d'énergie renouvelable
  • Poste basé à Perth, Brisbane ou Montréal
  • Nouveaux postes de base dans le domaine des énergies renouvelables où votre expertise peut briller

À propos du rôle

Rio Tinto a récemment créé une équipe dédiée pour fournir des solutions d'énergie renouvelable dans nos principales juridictions. Rio Tinto Energy Development (RTED) se concentre sur l'accélération du développement des actifs énergétiques futurs et sur la garantie d'une option de développement d'énergie renouvelable de haute qualité. L'accent mis par l'équipe sur la fourniture d'énergie verte permettra la décarbonisation des opérations industrielles existantes de l'entreprise et soutiendra la croissance future de Rio Tinto.

RTED comprend une équipe de projets d'énergie renouvelable centralisée qui travaillera avec les actifs en dehors de nos principales régions énergétiques où nous considérons les énergies renouvelables à la fois comme un levier de réduction et une fonction de croissance future pour l'avenir (Québec, Pacifique et Pilbara). Ces actifs en dehors des régions centrales ont devant eux des solutions d'énergie renouvelable détaillées et complexes et comprennent à la fois des actifs de croissance existants et nouveaux. L'équipe se consacre à soutenir les résultats de la réduction des énergies renouvelables et aidera les groupes de produits à prendre des mesures pour permettre une adoption et une exécution plus rapides des solutions d'énergie renouvelable. Il est important de noter que l'équipe est plus qu'un service de conseil et se tiendra aux côtés des Groupes de produits lorsque des décisions seront prises sur les opportunités renouvelables.

Pour renforcer cela, nous recherchons des conseillers principaux dans l'équipe des projets d'énergie renouvelable. Ces postes-clés peuvent être basés à Perth, Brisbane ou Montréal.

Les candidats, que nous recherchons, auront une expérience récente et prouvée dans la livraison de projets renouvelables, la création d'accords sur les énergies renouvelables et/ou la construction d'énergies renouvelables. Vous travaillerez aux côtés des équipes de site existantes, apportant une expertise approfondie aux négociations externes ou au développement d'actifs renouvelables internes, et tirerez parti de votre compréhension des limites de pénétration des énergies renouvelables.

Vous travaillerez en partenariat avec l'entreprise sur l'analyse des options (quantitatives et qualitatives) et démontrerez votre capacité d'exécution pour soutenir la livraison du projet et l'optionnalité à long terme.

Grâce à vos compétences d'influence, interpersonnelles et relationnelles, votre analyse et vos présentations feront partie intégrante de la création de solutions axées sur le commerce et de la communication efficace avec les principaux intervenants. Votre rôle jouera un rôle-clé dans l'obtention des meilleurs résultats renouvelables dans l'ensemble de nos actifs et dans la création d'une culture gagnante pour faire la différence.

L'intention de ces rôles est de livrer aux côtés des Groupes de produits, et le candidat retenu préparera et mènera des discussions avec le Groupe plus large sur les opportunités de réduction.

C'est un excellent moment pour rejoindre la compagnie dans des rôles clés, définir l'agenda et produire des résultats. Les personnes qui peuvent penser, agir et réussir, tout en conduisant le changement, en fournissant une orientation et en répondant aux besoins de l'entreprise pourront commencer ici et aller n'importe où.

Nous avons des opportunités en tant que Conseillers Principal- Commercial et Conseiller Principal – Technique.

Ce que nous offrons

Soyez reconnu pour votre contribution, votre réflexion et votre travail acharné, et rentrez chez vous en sachant que vous avez aidé le monde à progresser.

  • Un environnement de travail où la sécurité est toujours la priorité numéro un
  • Une culture soutenant les options de travail flexibles
  • Un poste permanent travaillant directement pour Rio Tinto
  • Un salaire de base compétitif reflétant vos compétences et votre expérience avec le programme incitatif annuel
  • Prestations médicales complètes, y compris une assurance maladie privée subventionnée pour les employés et la famille immédiate
  • Plan d'actionnariat attractif
  • Couverture d'assurance fournie par l'entreprise
  • Aide au développement de carrière et à l'éducation pour poursuivre vos ambitions techniques ou de leadership
  • Accès continu à un soutien en matière de santé et de bien-être médical adapté aux familles
  • Congé pour toutes raisons de la vie (vacances/annuel, congé parental payé, congé de maladie)

The job title is: Team Leader - Youth Navigation Portal (Mental Health).Further details:

About Marymead

Marymead is a well-respected, community-based, not-for-profit organisation that has provided a range of support services to children, young people and their families since 1967. Marymead now operates throughout the southern and western regional areas of NSW as well as the ACT with offices in Goulburn, Wagga Wagga, Young, Moruya, and Canberra. Marymead is now searching for an experienced team leader to lead and drive a new project in the Youth mental health space!

About the Team Leader position

Marymead are now working on an exciting new project in conjunction with ACT Health and the Office for Mental Health and Wellbeing to develop a dedicated online portal for children and young people to access mental health support and resources. Set to launch later this year, this unique model will provide an integrated source of information and easy access points for children and young people experiencing mental health challenges.

As the Team Leader during the development of the portal, you will be responsible for content review and development, contributing to the development of new procedures, participating in the testing of the Portal as well as recruitment, induction and training of new service delivery staff. You will have clinical leadership and line management responsibilities, as well as accountability for some direct service delivery. Once the portal goes live, you will be responsible for the day-to-day operations of the service, providing leadership to team members, direct service delivery, monitoring progress and supporting service delivery staff with the complexities of delivering the service.

The Portal will be operational between midday and 11pm, Monday to Sunday. The core hours for the Youth Portal Team Leader position will span across Monday to Sunday with work hours and the potential to work from home to be negotiated with the successful applicant. This position is a full-time or part-time contract until June 2023 with the possibility of extension.

As a non-profit employer, Marymead is able to provide staff with access to generous salary packaging arrangements and you will also have access to free parking at our Narrabundah site!

To be successful for this position you will possess:

  • Degree in Psychology, Social Work, Counselling or equivalent;
  • Registration as psychologist, social worker, counsellor or equivalent;
  • ACT Working with Vulnerable People Clearance and NSW Working with Children Check;
  • Demonstrated experience in building and managing teams with proven leadership skills;
  • Knowledge of early intervention for mental health and trauma-informed care and practice
  • Experience with Salesforce and Penelope would be advantageous

How to apply

On-Premises Technology Support:

As the Head of Operations, you will play a critical role in overseeing the efficient and reliable operation of our data center facilities. Drawing upon your extensive experience in critical facilities management and MEP background, you will lead a team dedicated to ensuring the optimal performance, safety, and reliability of our infrastructure.

So who is Reckon?

We’re a modern tech company that helps people and businesses change the way they operate – for the better. We specialise in software, but we’re more than just a technology company. Our experienced people, services and solutions provide businesses, accountants and lawyers with the tools and support they need. Our humble beginnings as an Australian start-up means we celebrate the entrepreneurial spirit of small business and spotlight the work of their advisors. The art of accounting is the cornerstone of our business. We’re proud of our collaborative, inclusive, and vibrant culture. We take care of ourselves, our teams, our customers, and our community.

 

Make a difference - So what is the role? 

Reckon is looking for a highly motivated Senior Developer to help lead the development of our next generation cutting edge products. Working in the Practice Management squad, you’ll have a focus on delivering the backend business logic of one of our core applications. We’ve built out a distributed architecture on top of a Kafka event driven architecture, and you’ll be heavily involved in building this out.

The first part of the system includes a series of GraphQL endpoints written in Typescript which is utilized by both our frontend and our Api partners. The second, building out a set of containerized Java and .net Core applications that act as Kafka producers and consumers. In the course of building out these applications, you’ll be dealing a lot with MySql, DynamoDb, ElasticSearch and the whole gamut of AWS services.

In addition to writing the backend, if you want, you’ll get exposure to building out the ReactJS frontend with our new design system tooling as well. We’re really happy with the way our system is coming together and want a motivated developer to help us build out these new applications.

This role is based in Auckland, with just two mandatory days in office and work from home rest of the days.

This role requires a focus on delivery of products that meet business requirements that become solutions and services Reckons customers will depend on every day. Ideal candidates will be comfortable working in a collaborative cross-functional team and being responsible for a whole application stack end to end.

Successful candidates will be those who want to challenge themselves to build great things.

Essential Skills

  • 5+ years’ previous experience in a Developer role or similar
  • Strong knowledge of Node.js (Serverless, micro services)
  • AWS experience (or Azure), including AWS Lambda (or Azure Functions)
  • Familiar with various design and architectural patterns
  • The ability to learn new technologies, take responsibility for the software you write all the way to production including strong focus on testing

Ideally you'll have

Dyson solves the problems others choose to ignore, developing disruptive technologies requiring even more complex electronics to deliver an increasing product portfolio. We are growing fast, and our ambition is boundless - more products, more locations, and more people.

The Senior Electronics Engineer role involves specification, design, and test of the electronic circuits for new and pioneering consumer appliance products within Dyson's Haircare category. As a member of the RDD Global Hardware - Haircare Electronics Team based in Malaysia Development Centre, you will work in multi-disciplinary global project teams to develop and deliver the electronics for Haircare products. And with a vibrant culture, the latest devices and a relaxed dress code reflecting our engineering spirit, it's an exciting team environment geared to fuelling and realising ambition.

담당하게 될 업무는 다음과 같습니다.

당신이 우리 국민들이 지원받고 있음을 느끼고 그들의 지식과 경력을 발전시킬 수 있도록 돕게하기 위하여 , 근무환경에 성공적으로 안착할 수 있도록 국회 서비스 안내 및 교육과 함께 지속적인 학습 및 자기 계발기회를 제공받을 것입니다.

  • Twelve Month contract | 38 hours per week

  • Make a meaningful difference to the lives of Australians in need!

Life at Mission Australia

When you join the team at Mission Australia, you become part of a community who are determined to end homelessness and ensure people in need can thrive. United by our Christian purpose and values, we stand together with anyone who needs us, for as long as they need us. Find out more about us and our purpose.

Your Opportunity

The Family Preservation Program (formerly known as Brighter Futures) provides targeted support to vulnerable children aged 0 -17 and families to prevent their issues from escalating. We currently have a vacancy for a skilled Case Manager to join our dynamic and motivated team.

A component of your role will be providing home visits to families in Albury and surrounding areas. This program makes a real difference in children's and their families lives. In this rewarding role you will provide targeted support to vulnerable children and families to ensure that children are healthy and safe and families provide safe, nurturing environments.

Although this is not an identified position, we strongly encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people to apply.

Your key responsibilities will to:

  • Provide intensive case management to families with children and young people.
  • Focus on parental vulnerability, specifically the impact of domestic violence, mental health issues, drug or alcohol misuse.
  • Support parents to implement strategies and develop the necessary skills and resources.
  • Deliver sessional, group based and issues focused parenting programs to enhance parents' competence.
  • Facilitate access to quality children's services to assist families to achieve healthy child development.
  • Work in partnership with DCJ to engage families who are at Risk of Significant Harm.
  • Provide on-call services for the program when required.
