  • Tertiary qualifications and/or relevant experience in the human services industry

  • Knowledge and understanding of issues facing vulnerable families and their children.

Before starting work with us, you will need to undertake a national police history check, qualifications, and referee checks, and have a clearance to work with children/vulnerable people.


Our culture

Our innovative and inclusive culture will ensure you feel valued at Mission Australia as you help Australians in need and develop in your career.


We're committed to the safety and wellbeing of each other and the people we serve.

Click 'Apply' and send your application today!

The job title is: Information Designer.Further details:

Job Ref: 36550

Does translating data and analysis through beautiful design make you happy? Are you an information design guru with a track record of delivering visualisation that makes a difference? Would you like to work for an agency that has supported millions of New Zealanders through the disruption of COVID-19? 

This could be the job for you.

Who we are:

The role of the Strategy and Insights group is to lead the development and implementation of the Ministry’s strategy by creating insights for effective decision making, focusing resources on the right investments, and understanding and evaluating performance.

The role:

The primary role of the Information Designer is to be a data narrative and visualisation leader within the Strategy and Insights Group. You’re here for your design and translation expertise - you’ll understand data concepts, but you don’t need to be on the data tools.

You’ll work with analysts across the group to ensure insights, analytics, and complex concepts are translated to a range of audiences in a compelling and visually engaging way. The value that analytics teams generate is only realised if people can understand the output produced. Work may be presented in the form of executive overviews, visual data explainers, technical reports or interactive visualisations. This will mean being able to communicate clearly to senior managers, Ministers, the general public and to workers on the front line, through good design and narrative.

You will also develop other members of the group to build their information design capability, providing advice as well as producing reusable templates or products. You will balance proactive upskilling of the wider group with responsive support for quick turnaround requests.

You will have:

  • Ability to think critically, with an inquisitive, questioning mind – you see the power in data and the story it can tell
  • Relevant tertiary qualification (particularly, Graphic Design, Information Design or Data Journalism), or equivalent experience
  • Strong portfolio of previous work that demonstrates technical graphic design and data visualisation expertise
  • You’re comfortable talking data with technical experts
  • Able to work with ambiguity and deliver results across multiple projects in a fast-changing environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to write to a high standard (clear, accurate, concise, appropriate to the audience).


How to apply:

Please apply online with your CV and cover letter via the "apply" button. A position description is available below.

Applications close Friday 12th February 2021

The job title is: Registered Nurse Balranald.Further details:

This position qualifies for a Recruitment Incentive Package up to the value of $10,000 (pro-rata part-time/temporary positions less than 18 months), and a reoccurring Annual Retention Bonus valued up to $10,000 (pro-rata part time), under the NSW Health Rural Health Workforce Incentive Scheme.

This scheme recognises the role key health workers play in enabling the delivery of rural and remote health services, and aims to provide incentives over and above award entitlements, to attract and retain staff in these areas.

Packages may consist of family and compassionate travel assistance, an upfront Rural Recruitment Cash Bonus upon appointment, contributions to professional development, utility reimbursements and study assistance, in addition to relocation benefits and accommodation assistance.

To recognise ongoing service in this role, once the successful candidate has served a qualifying period, they will become entitled to a reoccurring Annual Retention Bonus valued up to $10,000 (as taxable income).

For more information, please discuss incentive options with the contact person for this role.


Employment Type: Permanent Full Time (multiple positions available)
Position Classification: Registered Nurse
Remuneration: $70049.73 - $98351.39 + Super
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: REQ443821
Location: Balranald NSW (1-hour from Swan Hill VIC)


Balranald truly is a town like no other with a supportive community that will welcome you with open arms. We can't wait to see you! Take a quick look at "Living and Working" in the Far West. 

What you'll be doing
  • Work in one of the Far West LHD's newer, modern facilities in a beautiful location 100 metres from the Murrumbidgee river
  • Join a supportive, multi-disciplinary healthcare team who are very welcoming and embrace all newcomers to the hospital family
  • Develop your skills & progress your career working across a wide stream of specialties in a smaller, rural hospital
  • A doctor is never far away with a co-located GP practice
  • Excellent training and education opportunities to advance your nursing skills
  • Make a real, meaningful difference to health outcomes for the local community

What we offer

  • Salary packaging (pay less tax!) and enjoy up to $9K for living expenses + $2.6K meal and entertainment
  • Paid Allocated Day Off (ADO) Every Month
  • Isolation & climate allowance
  • Access to the in-house gym
  • Support through advanced education & training
  • A comfortable country lifestyle that supports balance & wellbeing

About the Far West LHD

The Far West Local Health District is one of 15 LHDs under NSW Health, providing high quality public health services to the communities in far west NSW.

Key to our success of course, is our people. Our workforce is inclusive and diverse. We employ well over 800 clinicians and support staff across our 9 health facilities in Broken Hill, Balranald, Dareton, Ivanhoe, Menindee, Tibooburra, Wentworth, White Cliffs and Wilcannia.

In the Far West LHD, we are working together to make a real difference to the health outcomes for our communities.

We encourage you to consider joining our friendly team for a meaningful and rewarding career in rural and remote healthcare.

About Balranald

Balranald is a beautiful rural town on the banks of the Murrumbidgee River. It has a friendly atmosphere with great venues for barista coffee, a well renowned bakery and discovery centre. A short drive takes you to the scenic larger town of Swan Hill for shopping, a great swimming pool and art centre. Balranald offers amazing food at the local RSL and to die for take away Pizza. Balranald Shire is home to the spectacular Yanga National Park and World heritage listed Mungo National Park, rich in Aboriginal history. Surrounded by five of NSW’s most iconic rivers (the Murray, Lachlan, Wakool, Edward & Murrumbidgee), the town provides an ideal location for boating, fishing, kayaking and other water sports.



How to apply 
To be considered for this position, please ensure you address the selection criteria in the application as thoroughly as possible.

  • Current nursing/midwifery registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) with postgraduate qualification in relevant field to position or willingness to undertake.
  • Recent remote and Emergency Department clinical experience, including current Advanced Life Support Accreditation.
  • Demonstrated application of professional and ethical boundaries to the delivery of patient care in the context of a multi-disciplinary team.
  • Demonstrated application of evidence based practice and critical thinking to advocate for and implement individualised person centred care patient care.
  • Demonstrated capacity to interact with others in a personable and professional manner and personally resolve conflicts when they arise.
  • Demonstrated commitment to work and partner with Aboriginal and Torres Strait, Islander patients and families and employees to enhance health outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander clients.
  • Evidence of participation in own professional development and commitment to maintaining competence and enhancement of skills, and willingness to apply and share professional expertise with colleagues.
  • Demonstrated effective interpersonal skills, excellent written and verbal communication skills within a multidisciplinary team.

Need more information?
  1) Click here for the Position Description
  2) Find out more about applying for this position
For role related queries or questions contact Michelle Straub on Michelle.Straub@health.nsw.gov.au

Applications Close: 

#RuralHealthIncentives

Far West Local Health District is committed to building a workplace culture that values diversity. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and encourage people with disability, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander to apply for position

Clough has an exciting opportunity for an Electrical & Instrumentation Commissioning Specialist to join the Waitsia Team in Dongara! Reporting to the Commissioning Superintendent you will be responsible for the safe, efficient, and technical aspects of commissioning all electrical and instrumentation equipment.

The Waitsia Gas Project is ranked one of the largest gas fields ever discovered onshore in Australia and Stage 2 involves further development of the gas field with new wells and a new production facility. Clough is currently undertaking the Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) scope of the development, near Dongara, Western Australia.

Who we are

We are a pioneering project delivery company. We harness innovative engineering and construction solutions to improve peoples' lives today and tomorrow.

We deliver high performing assets for the energy, resources and infrastructure industries, underpinned by a dedication to innovation, sustainability and getting the job done safely and efficiently. Together with our parent company, Webuild, we are delivering some of Australia's largest projects.

Courageous. Innovative. Passionate. Creative. These are just a few words that describe you.

  • To coordinate Electrical & Instrumentation commissioning preparation and activities for all electrical scope of work
  • Write and give input to the creation of Electrical Commissioning Procedures

  • Ensure all work is performed to Australian Standard, Legislation and project standards

SG Support is the world’s largest donor management partner for non-profits and non-governmental organisations. Specialising in the fundraising subscription model, SG Support aims to take away non-profits’ administrative burden of finding, managing and maintaining donors – so that they can focus on their mission. A proud partner of over 70 international and local non-profits in 14 countries. Check us out at: www.sgsupport.com

Department        : Contact Centre

Reporting to       : Contact Centre Manager

Location              : Bangkok (Asoke)

If you're gifted with the art of conversation and can sell anything to anyone, then a career in telesales is calling your name—this is the opportunity you've been waiting for!

The 225 hectare (500+ acre) ecosanctuary is a ground-breaking conservation project that has reintroduced 18 species of native wildlife back into the area, some of which were previously absent from mainland New Zealand for over 100 years. 

Ka riro māu e ārahi ā mātau hōtaka ako katoa, me ngā huarahi whai wāhi a ngā rōpū mahi ki te pāpori, arā ko ngā iwi mana whenua, ngā hoa mahi tahi, ngā kaitautoko, te hunga e whai panga mai ana, ngā manuhiri me te hapori whānui. Ka whakahaere koe i tētahi rōpū kaiwhakaako, kaiwhakarite hōtaka kia whakawhiwhi kaupapa hiranga, whai wāhi hoki e hono atu ai te tangata ki te taiao, ka whakarite huarahi mō te reanga hou o Aotearoa kia hangā he anamata taiao. Ka whakawhiwhi hoki koe i ētahi tohutohu, ārahitanga, aronga rautaki hoki, puta noa i Te Māra a Tāne, hei tautoko i ngā mahi hei whakanoho mai i te ao Māori me te mātauranga Māori ki roto i ngā whakahaere o ia rā, kia whakatipuria hoki ngā mahinga ngātahi ki ngā iwi mana whenua me ngā tāngata whenua e tutuki ai ngā kawenga a Te Māra a Tāne ki raro i Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

Kei te rapu mātau I tētahi tangata e whai wheako ana mō ngā mahinga ngātahi, mō te tautoko whai wāhi mai, mō ngā mahi whakarārata kaimātakitaki i ngā rāngai ahurea, whakatoitū taiao, huamoni kore hoki. Me whai wheako hoki mō ngā mahi hei whakahaere i tētahi rōpū pukumahi. Ka whai pūkenga koe, ka whai āheitanga ki te reo Māori, ngā tikanga me te kawa, ka whakamahi i ēnei  hei tautoko i te manawanui o Te Māra a Tāne ki te ao Māori me te mātauranga Māori, arā kia whakatōkia haere ēnei hei wāhanga nui ki roto i te ahurea me ngā mahi o te whakahaere.

About the Role:

Spotless Facilities Services provides a comprehensive range of facilities management services to the New Zealand Defence Force (NZDF) sites in the lower North Island and the Canterbury, supporting Army and Air Force operations.

We are seeking a HSE Advisor to work with our NZDF Defence team based at Waiouru, who will play a key role in ensuring the safe delivery of facilities services to our customer. Reporting to the Senior HSE Advisor - Defence, you will be a proven health and safety leader, with a strong commitment to safe work practices and building a proactive Zero Harm culture.

On a daily basis:

You will lead our site based HSE activity and support our site teams and subcontractors with solid technical advice, safety planning, monitoring and implementation. Your ability to consult with, and encourage our staff, subcontract partners and customers in providing healthy and safe operating environments is paramount.  You will achieve this through identifying, assessing, eliminating and controlling risks and hazards therefore driving a successful Zero Harm culture across the sites.

Additionally, you will lead HSE investigations, maintain the site Facilities Maintenance Safety Management Plan (FMSMP), audit site HSE systems and processes and lead site safety meetings. You will work alongside the broader HSE team at other Defence sites and champion your site health and safety representatives.

This role is critical to our successful delivery of facilities services at our sites and we are looking for people with a passion for health and safety, an understanding of operational services as well as an ability to work at pace to deliver excellent outcomes.

There is an opportunity, following proven performance, to expand the role into a more regional position.  

Required Skills and Experience:

  • You will ideally hold a NZ Certificate in Workplace Health and Safety Practice (Level 4) or with our support be willing to achieve this qualification
  • You will possess a collaborative and practical approach and be able to build strong relationships with our customer, our site teams and our subcontractors
  • Good oral presentation skills accompanied by well-developed written and computer skills are a must for this role
  • Minimum 3 years’ HSE experience in a Contracting environment, construction industry or similar
  • Knowledge of the New Zealand legal framework for HSE including the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, Resource Management Act and industry guidelines and standards
  • Good problem solver, who is able to use their technical H&S knowledge to support our efforts to reduce our organisational risks
  • Analytical capability, with an ability to provide insights into site HSE performance
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Good stakeholder management ability
  • Minimum of Intermediate Microsoft Office suite skills
  • Current driver’s license

The Role:

Ascender is a leading payroll outsourcing provider in APAC, and we have a new Payroll Officer opportunity in our Melbourne (Southbank) office.

We are seeking an experienced and dynamic Payroll Officer to join our outsourced teams, working on one of our leading payroll products.

Our outsourced environment provides opportunities to deliver payroll services with a team-based approach, offering diversity, learning opportunities and long-term career paths that can't be found in in-house payroll roles.

This is an ideal opportunity for an experienced Payroll Officer looking to broaden their exposure and skillset.

  • Provide accurate and timely payroll services including end-to-end volume payroll processing, end of month payroll balancing & reporting, end of year payroll balancing & reporting including Single Touch Payroll reconciliation and
  • Complete customer requests such as terminations, adjustments and classifications changes.
  • Monitor and respond to payroll enquiries
  • Maintain personnel data and customer support databases to ensure systems reflect current information.
  • Attend team meetings and provide feedback and input on operational issues.

  • Great office locations and a vibrant team culture where people come first.


About Us

Ascender is a leader in providing payroll and HR software solutions in the Asia Pacific region. For over 30 years, we have focused on the prosperity of our clients: growing their businesses, enriching their lives, and shaping their future.

We help our clients put their people first to unlock the full potential of their workforce.

On 1 March 2021, Ascender was acquired by Ceridian, a global leader in human capital management technology that provides human resources, payroll, benefits, workforce management, and talent management functionality. With the acquisition of Ascender, Ceridian now serves a combined 1,500 customers and 2.5 million employees across 30 countries in the APJ region.

The acquisition is an exciting milestone in Ceridian and Ascender's journey to scale and accelerate global growth.

The job title is: International Student Adviser.Further details:
Help Swinburne meet its best-practice legislative welfare, safety and support obligations through outstanding customer service.

About the Job
In this role, we will expect you to assist Swinburne international students by providing the most pertinent and up to date safety, community and Swinburne support information needed to enable international students to succeed in their studies and live with confidence in Australia.

With a customer-service focus, you will provide support services to international students studying Swinburne’s programs in Australia. The International Student Advisor’s provide operational input to the development and implementation of pro-active activities and events to ensure the most appropriate support for international students throughout their lifecycle with Swinburne. The team also provides best practice critical incident support for students and their families if an unfortunate illness or accident should affect them.

About Swinburne University of Technology
Swinburne is a multi-sector university of science, technology and innovation with more than 54,000 students and 5,000 staff globally. We offer postgraduate, undergraduate, vocational education and online education to provide students with a variety of work-relevant pathways. Our mission is to be a world-class university, creating economic and social impact through science, technology and innovation. We aim to deliver future-ready learners, research with impact and innovative enterprise.

About you
To be successful in the role, you will have:
• A degree with subsequent relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of relevant experience and/ or education/ training
• Experience in supporting international students with a strong customer-service focus, demonstrated cultural sensitivity and strong understanding of cross-cultural communication
• Experience in developing practical problem-solving solutions to guide positive outcomes
• Experience in the development, coordination and promotion of a range of student focused activities and events
• Highly developed written(using MS Office suite), verbal and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to tailor different styles to diverse audiences
A full list of selection criteria is available within the position description.

Benefits
To find out more about the extensive range of benefits offered to Swinburne employees please visit Careers at Swinburne

How to apply and further information
Please submit your application by clicking on the ‘Apply’ link (where you will be redirected back to Swinburne's site to apply), and submit a resume, cover letter and a response to the Key Selection Criteria, as listed in the position description.

For further information not clarified in the position description, contact Desma Smith, (Associate Director, International Student Advisory) on dssmith@swin.edu.au.

Should you require further support for an interview due to special needs or consideration, please contact our Diversity Manager, Maree Norden, on inclusion@swin.edu.au. For support or queries related to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander employment, please contact DeadlyCareers@swin.edu.au

If you are experiencing technical difficulties with your application, please contact the Recruitment team on staffrecruitment@swin.edu.au

Agency enquiries will not be accepted for this position.

Swinburne is a large and culturally diverse organisation. We are proud to be recognised by the Workplace Gender Equality Agency as an Employer of Choice for women for 10 years in a row and of key initiatives such as our Pride@Swinburne Strategic Action Plan and our Reconciliation Action Plan. Equity and diversity are integral to our 2025 vision to be a world class university creating social and economic impact through science, technology and innovation.

Applications close at 5pm on Wednesday 30th June 2021.Country Codes: AUS.Salary information: nan.

The job title is: Postdoctoral Fellow in Computational Social Science (2 Positions).Further details:
Job Description

Candidates will have expertise in one or more of the following areas: statistical modelling; big data analytics; machine learning; natural language processing; network science; survey/experimental methods; causal inference; econometrics.

Qualifications

PhD in a discipline closely related to computational social science by date of appointment, with evidence of interdisciplinary research applying computational methods to the social sciences. This includes but is not limited to social science disciplines (sociology, political science, communication, economics etc.) or computer science and related disciplines (information science, data science, computational physics etc.)
Evidence of successful teaching in methods or theory.

Responsibilities

This is a full-time position for 2 years. The incumbent is expected to teach 2 modules related to computational methods per year (50%) and work with existing faculty members in pursuing computational social science research projects (50%). The incumbent will also contribute towards publishing top-tier journal articles and curriculum development in computational communication. The incumbent should expect to work with multiple projects and faculty advisors. The anticipated start date is 1 January 2023 prior to the beginning of the semester in January 2023.

Application Instructions

Interested applicants are required to submit a complete application dossier as listed below for full consideration. Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.
1. NUS Personal Data Consent Form for Job Applicants (You may download the file via this link http://www.nus.edu.sg/careers/files/NUS-Personal-Data-Consent-for-Job-Applicants.pdf) [link removed]
2. Full CV: academic and employment history, degrees obtained, scholarships and awards, post-doctoral and clinical/ residency training (where applicable), other study and research opportunities, Name of PhD supervisor, etc.
3. Scanned copies of academic certificates and transcripts
4. Documents relating to research

  • A statement (max of 3 pages) of major accomplishments in research, citing up to five research, citing up to five significant publications, creative work or other scholarly contribution, and explaining their significance.
  • Sample copies of these contributions should be provided (in the case of books, reviews should be provided).
  • A complete list of publications
  • Evidence of impact, e.g. citations (excluding self-citations)
  • Evidence of international visibility, e.g. invitations to speak, major keynotes and plenary addresses, elected membership in professional and learned societies, membership on editorial boards of leading journals.
  • Research awards

5. Documents relating to service activities and impact

  • At Department/Faculty/University levels
  • To the international academic community
  • To national and international agencies
  • Documents relating to education (including the supervision of junior researchers), if applicable

6. Teaching Portfolio

  • A preface (maximum 300 words) that makes the case for your appointment. This should be highly distilled summary of your key contributions to student learning and educational leadership, guided by your teaching philosophy.
  • A Teaching Statement that focuses on evidence of student learning and educational leadership (if applicable). Note that the Teaching Statement, together with documents on research (where applicable) and service contributions should be 3-5 pages. Examples of consideration that can guide the candidate in making a case for teaching impact and leadership, with a focus on self, students, others, scholarship, future plans.
  • Samples of teaching evaluation reports (including the highest and lowest scores achieved)

7. Diversity Statement
8. A list of FOUR Referees (including one from the applicant's PhD or post-doctoral advisor/supervisor). Referees are to submit their letters directly to cnmcareer@nus.edu.sg.

Covid-19 Message

At NUS, the health and safety of our staff and students are one of our utmost priorities, and COVID-vaccination supports our commitment to ensure the safety of our community and to make NUS as safe and welcoming as possible. Many of our roles require a significant amount of physical interactions with students/staff/public members. Even for job roles that may be performed remotely, there will be instances where on-campus presence is required.

Taking into consideration the health and well-being of our staff and students and to better protect everyone in the campus, applicants are strongly encouraged to have themselves fully COVID-19 vaccinated to secure successful employment with NUS.

More Information

Organization: Arts & Social Sciences

Department : Communications And New Media

Employee Referral Eligible: No

Ipsos Australia has been commissioned to conduct the NSW Household Travel Survey by Transport for NSW.

To ensure the ongoing success of the project, we are seeking committed casual field interviewers. As a member of the team, you will play a vital role in the delivery and collection of surveys materials and completion of face-to-face travel surveys on behalf of the Transport for NSW, around the Newcastle/Hunter Region.

Paid training will be provided.

Benefits

  • $37.13 per hour for fieldwork
  • Kilometres travelled paid at $0.95 per km
  • Fully paid training
  • Approximately 12-20 hours per week, 1-2 weeks per month

Requirements – Your main responsibilities will include:

  • Recruitment to Travel Survey: You will be responsible for recruiting eligible respondents to participate in the study, distributing GPS devices to agreeing participants, ensuring that they understand the purpose and importance of their responses, and scheduling appointments to complete an in-person interview and pick up devices.
  • Personal Interview and Collection: You will diligently conduct face-to-face interviews, collect the GPS devices from participants, and ensure accuracy and completeness of every survey.

To excel in this role, we are looking for individuals who possess the following qualities:

  • Commitment: We need team members who are dedicated and reliable during the fieldwork period
  • Attention to Detail: Accuracy is crucial when collecting data. You should strive to ensure all surveys are completed correctly and in full.
  • Excellent Communication Skills: You will interact with participants on a regular basis, so effective communication skills are essential. The ability to explain the purpose of the study clearly and address any queries or concerns is important.
  • Professionalism: As representatives of Ipsos and Transport for NSW, professionalism is paramount. You should maintain a positive and respectful attitude towards participants and always uphold ethical standards.

You will also require the following:

  • Available to work on weekends and (less-frequently) some weekdays:
  • Saturday and Sunday, or
  • Have availability to work several days Wednesday to Sunday.
  • Additional Tuesday shifts also available.
  • Available to work from 28th October.
  • A mobile phone, a current driver’s licence and have access to a reliable vehicle
  • The right to work in Australia
  • Be comfortable using smart devices (e.g., tablets)

Sales, Field, or Census interviewing experience would be beneficial, but not essential as full training will be provided

This job is ideal for semi-retired people, students, or people looking for extra income, and offers flexible working hours.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants are strongly encouraged to apply.

By joining our team, you will contribute to the success of this important project and make an impact on our understanding of travel habits in NSW. We look forward to welcoming you on board!

The job title is: Senior Officer, KYC & AML Specialist (Advisory), Group Wholesale Banking.Further details:
About UOB

United Overseas Bank Limited (UOB) is a leading bank in Asia with a global network of more than 500 branches and offices in 19 countries and territories in Asia Pacific, Europe and North America. In Asia, we operate through our head office in Singapore and banking subsidiaries in China, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, as well as branches and offices.

Our history spans more than 80 years. Over this time, we have been guided by our values — Honorable, Enterprising, United and Committed. This means we always strive to do what is right, build for the future, work as one team and pursue long-term success. It is how we work, consistently, be it towards the company, our colleagues or our customers.

About the Department

The Wholesale Bank function operates a dynamic business model that provides financial services and solutions to help our clients achieve their strategic business objectives. Our mission is to become the premier-provider of banking services and solutions for Asia-based commercial banking companies (small medium enterprises), large corporations, financial institutions as well as multinational corporations. Our coverage teams work in full alignment with specialised teams across Transaction Banking, Investment Banking, Global Markets and Group Retail to deliver seamless solutions to our clients.

Job Responsibilities

The selected candidate will be a part of the team providing advisory guidance in compliance with relevant AML/CFT and Sanctions requirements pertaining to Commercial Banking customers due diligence (CDD) program. This includes incorporating customer identification and verification (ID&V), know your customer (KYC) and anti-money laundering (AML) principles are in place, in meeting regulatory requirements and helping to grow the business.

The role entails:
- AML and KYC related advisories
o Ensure timely follow-up to queries from business unit
o Accurate and up to date KYC / CDD information is provided to business unit
o Act as the liaison contact between business unit and Compliance on all AML/CFT and Sanctions matters.
o Follow up on directives from Compliance to ensure business unit adherence
o Timely clearance of alert screening hits encountered by business unit
o Ensure oversight on segment transfer customers that all CDD documents are accurate, valid and in correct order

- Compliance Escalations
o Summarize case and issues of concern, with appropriate escalation to Compliance for further concurrence
o Track and ensure such escalations are handled promptly by business unit, post Compliance's endorsement

- Ensure data accuracy in systems and documentations
- Extraction of data from worksheets and reports for distribution to respective Business segments for necessary follow-up actions
- Assisting BUs to respond to various CDD enquiries, which may originate from the local authorities or from correspondent banks, over client's profile
- Assisting the Team Leader in providing regular statistics and presentations for updating to Senior Management
- Participating in ad-hoc assignments and projects, e.g., audit, user acceptance testing etc. where required

Job Requirements
  • Tertiary holder and above
  • Prior working experience in KYC roles, will be advantageous
  • Detail-oriented, yet able to think flexibly and independently to resolve problems
  • Maintaining a high degree of knowledge in MAS 626 regulations and associated regulatory requirements for AML/CFT and Sanctions.
  • Emotionally mature and able to communicate maturely and independently with various stakeholders within the Bank
  • Comfortable with handling data, and able to perform functions on Excel, such as Vlookup, Pivoting and generating various graphs / charts, etc.
  • Attentive to details with a strong sense of interest in developing a career as a KYC specialist
  • Good command of both written and spoken English. The ability to speak / read additional languages is an advantage
Be a part of UOB Family

UOB is an equal opportunity employer. UOB does not discriminate on the basis of a candidate's age, race, gender, color, religion, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, or other non-merit factors. All employment decisions at UOB are based on business needs, job requirements and qualifications. If you require any assistance or accommodations to be made for the recruitment process, please inform us when you submit your online application.

The job title is: Senior Manufacturing Test Engineer.Further details:

Company description:

About us

Dyson began twenty one years ago with James Dyson and a handful of engineers questioning everyday products, thinking differently and making them better. We are now the world's number one vacuum cleaner manufacturer in the UK, US, Japan, Europe and Australasia.

We've even branched out to improving commercial technology that frustrates us. The Dyson Airblade hand dryer dries hands in ten seconds, it's also the most hygienic and energy efficient hand dryer available. And more recently a fan, Air Multiplier, with no blades or grille.

There are over 4000 in the world and we're all inventive and hugely passionate about what we do. At our Development Centre in Johor Bahru, Malaysia & Singapore there are almost 1600 of us, a mixture of engineers and support staff, we are Dyson people that are encouraged to think differently, challenge convention and be unafraid to make mistakes. Our teams there will rise to more than 2000 over the next 2 years.


Job description:

About the role

We are looking to hire a talented mechanical design engineer for the design and development of an ergonomic manufacturing test solution. This is a unique opportunity to demonstrate your engineering skills at the organizational level by working closely with R&D product development team and external test development suppliers in forming the objective and vision of a manufacturing test system.

In this role, you will be required to collaborate with R&D and external test development suppliers to determine manufacturing test system design requirements and the system architectural design to support "manufacturing testing" capabilities. You will be involved in the conceptual design of mechanical test equipment, evaluating proof of principle test, and detail design intended for business requirement in order to ensure that design specifications of a test system are met.

To be a successful as mechanical test equipment design engineer, you should be mechanically minded plus with some basic knowledge in electrical with strong analytical and critical thinking abilities. You should possess detailed knowledge of engineering and mechanical design principles and be able to find creative solutions to technical problems.


What we offer:

Requirements:

* Candidates must possess at a bachelor's degree in Mechatronic/Mechanical Engineering with at least 3-5 years of working experience in electronics manufacturing assembly environment with great knowledge and understanding of manufacturing test system.

*Proficiency with engineering design programs such as AutoCAD and/or Solidworks.

* Good understanding on pneumatic control system, servo motors, and manufacturing line automation system.

* Able to challenge the purpose and objective of test clearly.

* Sound knowledge of design, engineering principles and best practices.

* Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities in sustaining test system.

* Exceptional time management and organizational skills.

* Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.

* Attentive to detail and critically minded.

* The ability to stay abreast of advancements in technology and engineering design trends.

* Great engineering practices on subjects related to Dfx, DFMEA and PFMEA.

* Strong team player and able to drive technical deliverables of manufacturing test solution and able to highlight technical risk with mitigation plan.

* Knowledgeable in statistical process control (SPC) and data analysis for test optimization.

Benefits

Dyson Malaysia monitors the market to ensure we offer competitive salaries, management bonuses and pension contributions. Beyond that, you'll enjoy generous leave and medical care and insurance. But financial benefits are only the start of a career at Dyson. Leadership support and new opportunities abound, driven by regular dialogue and international training. And with a vibrant culture, the latest devices and a relaxed dress code reflecting our engineering spirit, it's an exciting team environment geared to progress, innovation and realising ambition.

#LI-DYSON

 
 

Required profile:

Main Duties/Responsibilities:

* Collaborate globally at early phase with R&D design teams to determine the purpose of mechanical test applications and test requirements.

* Generating test equipment specification involving system architecture concept, main block diagrams and bill of material for RFQ purpose.

* Conducting research to standardize test system design where it is feasible using best practices and engineering methods required for the mechanical test systems.

* Reviewing test supplier's technical proposal on test system design and optimizing design solution for ergonomic design and cost.

* Planning and executing mechanical designs using CAD, CAM, and 3D CAD programs.

* Overseeing the development and manufacturing of physical prototypes for testing.

* Documenting the design process, iterations, and test analytics.

* Liaising with RDD design engineers, manufacturing process engineers, contract manufacturers to ensure coherence.

* Drive engineering deliverables with great sense of urgency on any productivity issues related to the test and measurement system with the support of the respective cross functional teams internally and externally.

* Optimise manufacturing test time by streamlining manufacturing test script and simplicity of test system design.

* Driving continuous improvement plan through process capability study and using statistical tools such as CpK to optimize manufacturing test limits.

* Research and recommend new technologies to improve tester efficiency and manufacturing throughput.

* Work with project management team to deliver a reliable test solution on time.

* Qualifying and commissioning manufacturing test system by using Gauge R&R and or Gauge1.

* Collaborate with RDD in the early phase of product development and test strategy development.

The job title is: NUM 1 Community MHDA.Further details:

Employment Type: Permanent Full Time
Position Classification: Nurse Unit Manager Level 1
Remuneration: $118643.63 + Super
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: REQ372019
Location: Broken Hill NSW 2880

What you'll be doing

  • Provide nursing leadership to the Community MHDA service.
  • Assist with the development of less experienced staff by providing support, guidance and direction.
  • Create and maintain staffing arrangements which are in compliance with applicable awards and maintain adequate skill mix requirements for the service.

Incentives

  • 1 week extra paid annual leave per year
  • Salary packaging (pay less tax!)
  • Paid Allocated Day Off (ADO) Every Month
  • Isolation & climate allowance
  • Remote Area Housing Assistance Benefits
  • Employee Meal & Entertainment Card
  • Special rates at local gyms
  • Support through advanced education & training
  • A comfortable country lifestyle that supports balance & wellbeing

About Broken Hill

A true “Oasis in the Outback”, Broken Hill is a thriving regional town in far west NSW full of diversity, history and character. Being Australia’s first city to be Nationally Heritage Listed, Broken Hill is a culturally rich town with a vibrant art scene with over 20 galleries! The unique attractions, festivals and beautiful natural landscapes see tourists flock from all over, but the ones who stay quickly fall in love with the place and its liveability.

With a population just shy of 20,000, Broken Hill is small enough to allow for a relaxed country lifestyle, while big enough to provide all the desired facilities of a regional hub including major supermarkets and retail stores, excellent schools (7 primary & 2 high), multiple gyms & aquatic centre, well-known fast food franchises and a plethora of trendy restaurants, pubs and cafés.

The beautiful Murray-Riverina region is just 2.5 hours from Broken Hill, and after a short, 5-hour drive you can enjoy the beautiful Barossa Valley – South Australia’s internationally acclaimed wine region. For a town so unique, it’s really not that far away with just a short 1hr15m flight from Adelaide, a 2hr flight from Melbourne or a 2hr30m flight from Sydney.

Broken Hill truly is a town like no other with a supportive community that will welcome you with open arms. We can’t wait to see you soon!


Selection Criteria

  1. Current nursing/midwifery registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) with a minimum of 4 years post graduate experience and including 3 years Mental Health.
  2. Demonstrated effective interpersonal skills, excellent written, verbal communication skills with computer literacy and ability to use a variety of the NSW Health computer applications.
  3. Proven ability to create and maintain a positive workplace culture and articulate and achieve a vision for nursing services within a multidisciplinary community MHDA environment. The ability to negotiate resolutions and manage conflict.
  4. Demonstrated focus on service excellence through the ability to read and act on issues quickly, decisively and effectively and to apply and share professional expertise to enhance consumer care including actively contributing to the development of clinical practice in the unit by: Being involved in quality improvement initiatives Contribute to development of new clinical practices / policy Represent the unit at team / clinical meetings when required Ability to develop training packages of clinical specialty material
  5. Demonstrated ability to effectively lead, coach, mentor, encourage and guide others to enable them to reach their full potential and effectively adapt to ongoing change within a multidisciplinary group with broad clinical experience and knowledge by: Ability to act as a mentor to less experienced team members, including students and new graduate nurses and new team members of multidisciplinary team Provide clinical advice to less experienced experience nurses and other health professionals Act as a preceptor to new staff and students in the clinical area
  6. Knowledge and understanding of mental health issues within the perinatal period with preparedness to undergo any recommended further training in this area.
  7. Licence to drive a motor vehicle in NSW.

About the Far West LHD

The Far West Local Health District is one of 15 LHDs under NSW Health, providing high quality public health services to the communities in far west NSW. FWLHD has a mandate to provide the highest quality care and services to its communities using the latest clinical evidence and technological enablers. Our vision is to create excellence in rural and remote healthcare.

Key to our success of course, is our people. Our workforce is inclusive and diverse. We employ well over 800 clinicians and support staff across our 9 health facilities in Broken Hill, Balranald, Dareton, Ivanhoe, Menindee, Tibooburra, Wentworth, White Cliffs and Wilcannia. In the Far West LHD, we are working together to make a real difference to the health outcomes for our communities. We encourage you to consider joining our friendly team for a meaningful and rewarding career in rural and remote healthcare.

Position Classification: Registered Nurse
Remuneration: $67357.32 -$94568.44 + Super
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: REQ431501
Location: Broken Hill NSW

We really aren’t that far away - only 3 hours’ drive from Mildura, 5 hours from Adelaide or a short flight from anywhere in Australia with everything you need right at your front door!

Broken Hill truly is a town like no other with a supportive community that will welcome you with open arms. We can't wait to see you! Take a quick look at "Living and Working" in the Far West. What you’ll be doing


What you'll be doing

  • Provide specialist assessment, care planning, treatment, withdrawal management, case management and referral services to people experiencing drug and alcohol problems and collaborate in the further development and delivery of a comprehensive multidisciplinary drug and alcohol service.
  • Work collaboratively with clinical and non-clinical services to provide quality and appropriate care to drug and alcohol clients with co-existing mental health issues and disorders.
  • Provide drug and alcohol education and training, promotion and prevention activities for communities, key services and clients and carers.
  • Participate in clinical handover, clinical  supervision and clinical reviews, utilising outcome measures and consumer goals in the development of ongoing care plans  

What is on offer

  • 5 Weeks Annual Leave
  • Salary packaging (pay less tax!) + Meal Entertainment Card
  • Paid Allocated Day Off (ADO) Every Month
  • Isolation & climate allowance
  • Support through advanced education & training
  • A comfortable country lifestyle that supports balance & wellbeing

About the Far West LHD

The Far West Local Health District is one of 15 LHDs under NSW Health, providing high quality public health services to the communities in far west NSW. FWLHD has a mandate to provide the highest quality care and services to its communities using the latest clinical evidence and technological enablers. Our vision is to create excellence in rural and remote healthcare.

Key to our success of course, is our people. Our workforce is inclusive and diverse. We employ well over 800 clinicians and support staff across our 9 health facilities in Broken Hill, Balranald, Dareton, Ivanhoe, Menindee, Tibooburra, Wentworth, White Cliffs and Wilcannia. In the Far West LHD, we are working together to make a real difference to the health outcomes for our communities. We encourage you to consider joining our friendly team for a meaningful and rewarding career in rural and remote healthcare.

About Broken Hill

A true “Oasis in the Outback”, Broken Hill is a thriving regional town in far west NSW full of diversity, history and character. Being Australia’s first city to be Nationally Heritage Listed, Broken Hill is a culturally rich town with a vibrant art scene with over 20 galleries! The unique attractions, festivals and beautiful natural landscapes see tourists flock from all over, but the ones who stay quickly fall in love with the place and its liveability.

With a population just shy of 20,000, Broken Hill is small enough to allow for a relaxed country lifestyle, while big enough to provide all the desired facilities of a regional hub including major supermarkets and retail stores, excellent schools (7 primary & 2 high), multiple gyms & aquatic centre, well-known fast food franchises and a plethora of trendy restaurants, pubs and cafés.

The beautiful Murray-Riverina region is just 2.5 hours from Broken Hill, and after a short, 5-hour drive you can enjoy the beautiful Barossa Valley – South Australia’s internationally acclaimed wine region. For a town so unique, it’s really not that far away with just a short 1hr15m flight from Adelaide, a 2hr flight from Melbourne or a 2hr30m flight from Sydney.

Broken Hill truly is a town like no other with a supportive community that will welcome you with open arms. We can’t wait to see you soon!



How to apply  
To be considered for this position, please ensure you address the selection criteria in the application as thoroughly as possible.

  • Current unrestricted Registered Nurse registration with the Australian Health Professionals Regulation Agency (AHPRA) with a minimum of two years clinical experience working in the drug and alcohol sector.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and experience in drug and alcohol clinical practices and treatment interventions.
  • Demonstrated application of evidence based practice and critical thinking to advocate for and implement recovery oriented individualised person centred and trauma informed care to clients of the Drug and Alcohol service
  • Demonstrated commitment to work and partner with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander consumers and their families to enhance health outcomes.
  • Evidence of participation in own professional development and commitment to maintaining competence and enhancement of skills together with willingness to apply and share professional expertise with colleagues and students.
  • Demonstrated effective interpersonal skills including the verbal and written ability to communicate and consult with clients, family and/or carers and other health, community and welfare professionals together with intermediate computer skills including use of the Microsoft Office suite.
  • Demonstrated competence in the use of electronic information systems and the ability to maintain accurate medical records utilising appropriate documentation and entering data related to activity in a timely manner.
  • Current licence to drive in NSW

The Welcome Experience  

The Welcome Experience in Broken Hill connects you and your family with local people and local resources to help you settle in and feel at home in your new community faster.

Learn more at www.nsw.gov.au/welcomeexperience

Need more information?

Full-time EAP Counsellor, 12-month term: Deliver impactful, confidential support across two sites, helping employees thrive with solution-focused counselling.

The Role

Centacare is offering a full-time, 12-month fixed-term position for a dedicated and qualified EAP Counsellor to join our team at ACCESS Programs. In this role, you will report to the Manager and be responsible for providing short-term, solution-focused counselling to employees dealing with personal, family, or work-related challenges that affect their well-being and quality of life. You will work one day a week at our Elizabeth site and the remaining four days at our Adelaide head office. Flexibility is required, as you may need to work outside of normal hours based on business needs.

The key duties in this role will include:

  • Provide confidential and voluntary counselling services to employees through the EAP.
  • Assist employees in identifying problems and developing strategies for resolving personal, family, or work-related issues.
  • Utilize short-term, solution-focused counselling techniques to address a range of concerns.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality and privacy regarding all counselling sessions, ensuring that no information is disclosed to the employer unless explicitly requested and authorized in writing by the client.
  • Offer flexible counselling services, including out-of-hours support and sessions at various convenient locations.
  • Provide psychological interventions/counselling 

About You

You are a compassionate and experienced professional with a strong background in mental health counselling. You possess excellent interpersonal skills and have a deep understanding of the challenges employees face in balancing work, family, and personal life. You are committed to providing confidential, solution-focused support and can effectively navigate sensitive situations with professionalism and empathy.

 Essential Criteria

  • Degree qualification in Psychology or Social Work and membership of the relevant professional body AASW or APS
  • Minimum 5 years’ experience in clinical service delivery
  • Ability to participate in an on-call roster
  • Experience in counselling and therapeutic approaches

See attached Position Description for full details. 

Prior to receiving a formal offer of employment with Centacare, the following documents must be provided for this role:

  • Driver’s licence
  • Valid Working with Children Check (WWCC)

Loss Prevention Manager

We are looking for a Loss Prevention Manager to join our team.

This role is responsible for helping to ensure the safety of staff and customers at all times while managing all loss prevention / security related issues.

As the Loss Prevention Manager, you will be responsible for leading a culture in store that promotes preventing stock losses and theft from all avenues within our store.

The key task areas for this role are:

  • Handle all steps in the process relating to the apprehension and processing of shop lifters / customer theft.
  • Liaise regularly with other Store Security / Loss Prevention personnel.
  • Assist in preventing staff theft.
  • Regularly update to Owner Operator re loss prevention incidents and issues.
  • Liaise regularly with appropriate employees to identify steps and systems to reduce all loss (e.g. stock loss, loss through paperwork errors, customer theft and staff theft)
  • Manage door guard responsibilities – ensure all customers entering the store / site are acknowledged and greeted as appropriate to deter would-be shoplifters.  Ensure all contractors etc on site follow appropriate policies.
  • Ensure all appropriate paperwork is completed and maintained as required e.g. including but not limited to trespass notices / police reports / security reports.
  • Undertake regular store walks (internal and external) to identify potential security issues / concerns.
  • Liaise appropriately with external bodies e.g. Police/Mall Security to ensure all systems / processes are up to date and legally compliant. To also maintain relationship with appropriate community groups.
  • As required record appropriate customer complaints and follow up corrective actions if required.
  • Investigating stock discrepancies
  • Identifying loss patterns
  • Identifying and deterring suspicious behaviour
  • Being a health & safety champion
  • Reducing opportunities for theft
  • Ensuring a safe and secure store environment.

 

Loss Prevention is not just about theft, it's about making improvements to prevent it from occurring in the first instance.

Regional Supplier Quality Manager

Salary: Competitive and based on experience

Location: Bangkok

Keywords: Quality Management, Supplier Development, Problem Solving, Continuous Improvement, Interpersonal Collaboration, Chemical, Construction Material

This role offers the opportunity to monitor and enhance the supply base, ensuring that suppliers are providing top-quality products. The successful candidate will be responsible for monitoring supplier performance, evaluating corrective and preventive action responses, and performing audits. This is an exciting opportunity to work with a market leader known for its unique technology and focus on sustainability.

  • Chance to utilise your skills in quality management systems and supplier development

You will act as a crucial link between various departments such as procurement, local operations, R&D and our suppliers on all matters related to quality. Your responsibilities will include reporting all quality claims to suppliers, following up with structured problem-solving methods, qualifying global suppliers, enhancing supplier quality management processes, classifying and evaluating global suppliers, and developing new and existing suppliers within the region to meet our stringent quality expectations.

  • Act as the bridge between procurement, local operations, R&D and our suppliers on all quality-related topics

What you bring:

The ideal candidate for this Regional Supplier Quality Manager position brings a wealth of experience in quality management systems and supplier development. You have proven experience using problem-solving methodologies and tools such as 8D, 5-Why, Ishikawa etc., which you can apply effectively across diverse production processes (mechanical and chemical). Your competence in process quality and continuous improvement is matched by your strong moderation, influencing and conflict management skills. You have the ability to articulate the functions and value propositions of SQM clearly. Furthermore, your analytic thinking, project management, communication, interpersonal and intercultural collaboration skills are top-notch.

  • Proven knowledge in quality management systems and supplier development
  • Experience in problem-solving methodology and tools like 8D, 5-Why, Ishikawa etc.
  • Quick comprehension of diverse production processes (mechanical and chemical)
  • Competence in process quality and continuous improvement
  • Strong moderation, influencing and conflict management skills
  • Ability to articulate the functions and value propositions of SQM
  • Good skill set of analytic thinking, project management, communication, interpersonal and intercultural collaboration

Our client is a market leader known for its unique technology and strong focus on sustainability. The job title is: Senior Audience Insights Analyst.Further details:

  • 12-month fixed term contract
  • Sydney or Melbourne location


The safety and wellbeing of our employees and potential employees are important to us. Our external candidates will have the choice to either interview in our offices or via Zoom. Not only do we wish to protect the health and safety of our people, we want to assure candidates that there is no expectation from REA to meet face-to-face. A virtual interview will not adversely impact your application. If you have any questions or concerns, this can be discussed through the screening process.


We're REA

An Australian start-up success story we're quietly proud of.

From a garage in Melbourne to the global stage is an achievement we're humbled by. Our idea to put pictures of houses on the internet has blossomed since 1995, and we now have businesses across Australia, Asia, India and North America.

Our purpose is to change the way the world experiences property. No matter where you're at on your property journey, we're here to help on every step - whether that's buying, selling, renting or renovating.

Some of our brands include realestate.com.au, realcommercial.com.au, spacely.com.au, Flatmates.com.au, Smartline.com.au and Proptrack.com.

What we're doing

Analytics & audience data is at the heart of decision making and drives critical marketing decisions. We have scaled up our audience insights and analytics team in the Audience & Marketing division to transform and provide richer data stories and strategic insights across all our key consumer audience segments.

What the role is all about:

The primary focus for the Senior Audience Insights Analyst is to provide rich audience data insights for REA Group brands, including realestate.com.au and realcommercial.com.au.

The Senior Audience Insights Analyst will support the Audience & Marketing division and play a pivotal role in working closely with key stakeholders for customers in analysing data and providing insights to assist them to drive compelling audience stories for both internal and external purposes.

The role is a 12-month contract (maternity leave cover) with a possible opportunity for extension.


What you'll be doing

While there's a good chance no two days will be exactly the same, the key accountabilities for the Senior Audience Insights Analyst are:

  • Provide regular reporting, as required, to support our weekly, monthly and quarterly analysis, including preparing decks on audience performance and KPI, Board materials, etc.
  • Communicate insights regularly with key stakeholders and relevant teams including presentations.
  • Investigate data from a variety of sources to gain insights into consumer audience trends and behaviours and distil these data into reports and dashboards that assist the business.
  • Be at the forefront of competitor trends and insights, ensuring the business is kept informed.
  • Build the self-serve capability for key audience metrics and data sources.
  • Be the key point of contact for customer teams for audience data ensuring data is 100% accurate and sourced correctly.
  • Deliver data visualisation and reports for stakeholders (for internal and external use), creating holistic dashboards by pulling data from different data sources.
  • Work with the team to build a central resource for audience analysis and insights.
  • Manage ad-hoc data requests from customer teams and other internal stakeholders, prioritising accordingly.
  • Be the champion for internal processes and systems and identify process improvement.


Who we're looking for

The role is suitable for someone who has already developed great hands-on 'technical' skills in digital marketing and analytics.

  • Demonstrated experience in a data insights or reporting function in relation to digital audience.
  • Extensive experience in digital analytics tools that cover website and mobile usage (eg, Adobe Analytics, Google Analytics
  • Experience in database interrogation using SQL (intermediate) and BigQuery.
  • Advanced Excel skills including pivot tables, vlookup, charts and formulae.
  • Experience using business intelligence systems such as Tableau.
  • High analytical, logical, and critical thinker with an eye for detail.
  • Demonstrated experience in managing multiple projects at the same time, within tight deadlines.
  • Exceptional storytelling, visualisation, and stakeholder engagement skills to clearly communicate insights and explain complex analysis in an easy-to-understand way.
  • You are keen to understand audience trends and the stories that data can tell.
  • You are highly inquisitive with experience and a passion for solving problems.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to explain complex analysis in an easy-to-understand way.
  • Self-motivated with a positive attitude.
  • Strong attention to detail is essential.
  • Work productively in a fast paced and agile environment.


But we don't just look for someone based on their skills and expertise. It's our connection, acceptance and genuine care for each other that makes REA a great place to work. That means you also need to be:

  • Savvy minded and have the ability to think a little left of field / outside the box
  • A strong and creative communicator
  • Friendly, approachable and have good relationship management skills

The job title is: Disability Support Worker.Further details:

About the Organisation

Life Without Barriers is a leading social purpose, not for profit organisation of 8,000 employees working in more than 500 communities across Australia. We support children, young people and families, people with disability, older people and people with mental illness. We work with people who are homeless and refugees and asylum seekers.   

Empowering people with disability to live life the way they choose is at the heart of how Life Without Barriers has operated for over 25 years. This is an exciting opportunity to join our team and continue this mission. Support people with disability to have the choice, control, and independence to live their best life. If you’re passionate about inclusivity, respect, and making a meaningful difference, this is the career move for you.

We want to employ people who reflect the diversity of our clients to ensure we can support each client's individual needs and wants. We encourage people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander background and people with disability to apply.

About the role

We are looking for a Disability Support Worker to assist our male client in Chinchilla.  This is a casual position, where you will support our client to maintain his independence in accessing the community, attending appointments and supporting him in activities of daily living. You will need your own transport to get to work, and the client accesses taxi services to transport into the community. Our client is an intelligent and kind man, who enjoys good company and a good chat. Shifts are rotating fortnightly:

Week 1: Monday 12pm - 5pm, Friday 2pm - 5pm

Week 2: Monday 10am - 3pm, Friday 2pm - 5pm

Key Responsibilities

  • Community access and transport
  • Maintain and monitor Person Centred Plans
  • Track and document an individual’s progress through thorough record-keeping
  • Build rapport and collaborate effectively with the people we support and their families to establish positive relationships

Skills & Experience

  • Unrestricted Australian Drivers Licence and reliable vehicle
  • Current First Aid and CPR Certificate
  • Prior experience in the industry supporting clients with disability and/or relevant qualifications will be highly regarded

To be considered for and appointed to a position at Life Without Barriers, you must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 with a minimum of two (2) doses or hold a valid medical exemption certificate, in accordance with Life Without Barriers Employee COVID-19 Vaccination Policy. You will be required to provide evidence of your vaccination status during the recruitment process.

Successful candidates will be required to clear probity checks including National Criminal History Record Check and an NDIS Worker Screening Check.

Benefits

  • An opportunity to make a meaningful, positive impact in the lives of people with a disability within your local community
  • Casual pay rate from $40.26 per hour + Super
  • Get reimbursed per kilometre travelled in your own vehicle while you are working
  • Receive up to $15,900 of your annual salary tax free through salary packaging benefits
  • Access to discounts and benefits at selected retail outlets, cinemas, restaurants and more

How to Apply

Include your resume and covering letter in one document, click ‘Apply’ and follow the prompts. For any enquiries including persons with disability that require adjustments, contact Rianne Gifford at recruitment@lwb.org.au 

Applications close at midnight on Sunday 17th of December 2023

The job title is: Wellington isite Visitor Centre - Customer Service Consultant.Further details:

Do you love the Wellington region and all it offers? 

 

And want to share your enthusiasm and knowledge of our beautiful region with visitors… then we have an awesome opportunity for you. 

 

Come and join the Wellington isite Visitor Information Centre Team. We are looking for people to join our energetic and supportive team. 

 

As a Living Wage Employer – WellingtonNZ offers $26.00 per hour + 8% holiday pay.  

 

As this is a Casual position, you will not have set rostered hours, and there is no guarantee of the number of hours available each week. Our isite is open 7 days a week and only closes on Christmas Day. So, there are opportunities to work around your studies and other employment. Additional hours may become available when our permanent team members are on leave, and during our peak visitor periods. 

 

Ideally you are available to work one or both weekend days when shifts are available. 

 

About you

A genuine enjoyment in meeting new people every day and passionate about what the Wellington region offers. Experienced within a customer service environment, comfortable selling, confident problem solving, with a high-level of self-motivation. Friendly, welcoming and knowledgeable about the Wellington region.  

 

You will have worked in a fast-paced environment and can remain calm when the pressure is on. 

 

As we have visitors from all round the globe coming in to speak with us, we are also keen to hear from you if you speak another language, enjoy meeting new people and do not have any work experience.  

 

What you’ll do

You will help to provide the very best service to visitors from all over New Zealand and the world. Often as the first point of contact for travellers to the Wellington region, you will enjoy approaching and speaking with people you do not know, solving their problems, and selling our region. 

 

  • Making bookings on behalf of visitors, ticket sales and cash handling.  
  • Interacting with visitors and local operators over the phone, email, and in-person.  
  • Providing accurate information and advice to visitors.  
  • Keeping computer-based databases up to date.  
  • Ensuring the isite is presented in a clean and professional way. 

 
 

About us

WellingtonNZ is the agency tasked with ‘Creating a thriving Wellington Region for all’. Our organisation is shamelessly passionate about this wonderful region we call home and want to make it famous as the most creative place in New Zealand to live, work, visit and play. 

 

Check out some of the varied things we do in the video below. 

https://youtu.be/cupLikfIFz0 

 

Why people love it here
Every day meeting new people from all over the world! 

WellingtonNZ truly values its people and is committed to building an inclusive and collaborative culture where everyone can thrive, have fun and make a difference for the Wellington region. 
 
We have all the things you would expect from a great employer – the living wage, safe working environments, training for your role, and encouragement to bring your best self to work. 

 

How to apply
If our role description resonates with you and you want to be part of a diverse organisation all about making the Wellington region thrive, then take a moment to review the job description on our website and apply via Seek with your CV and cover letter telling us what you love about Wellington.  

Want to know more before applying? For a confidential conversation please call Jorge on 22 016 4319 or email them at people@wellingtonnz.com.   

Applications close at 5pm on Monday 23 October 2023. 

 

*Please note to be eligible for this opportunity, you’ll be based in the Wellington region and hold a valid Work Visa that allows you to be employed in New Zealand. We are not accredited with ImmigrationNZ and cannot provide sponsorship.

About Broken Hill

A true “Oasis in the Outback”, Broken Hill is a thriving regional town in far west NSW full of diversity, history and character. Being Australia’s first city to be Nationally Heritage Listed, Broken Hill is a culturally rich town with a vibrant art scene with over 20 galleries (more than pubs)! The unique attractions, festivals and beautiful natural landscapes see tourists flock from all over, but the ones who stay quickly fall in love with the place and its liveability.

With a population just shy of 20,000, Broken Hill is small enough to allow for a relaxed country lifestyle, while big enough to provide all the desired facilities of a regional hub including major supermarkets and retail stores, excellent schools (7 primary & 2 high), multiple gyms & aquatic centre, well-known fast food franchises and a plethora of trendy restaurants, pubs and cafés.

The beautiful Murray-Riverina region is just 2.5 hours from Broken Hill, and after a short, 5-hour drive you can enjoy the beautiful Barossa Valley – South Australia’s internationally acclaimed wine region. For a town so unique, it’s really not that far away with just a short 1hr15m flight from Adelaide, a 2hr flight from Melbourne or a 2hr30m flight from Sydney.

Broken Hill truly is a town like no other with a supportive community that will welcome you with open arms. We can’t wait to see you soon!

Our vision is to create excellence in rural and remote healthcare.

Key to our success of course, is our people. Our workforce is inclusive and diverse. In the Far West LHD, we are working together to make a real difference to the health outcomes for our communities. We encourage you to consider joining our friendly team for a meaningful and rewarding career in rural and remote healthcare.

About UOB

United Overseas Bank Limited (UOB) is a leading bank in Asia with a global network of more than 500 branches and offices in 19 countries and territories in Asia Pacific, Europe and North America. In Asia, we operate through our head office in Singapore and banking subsidiaries in China, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, as well as branches and offices.

Our history spans more than 80 years. Over this time, we have been guided by our values — Honorable, Enterprising, United and Committed. This means we always strive to do what is right, build for the future, work as one team and pursue long-term success. It is how we work, consistently, be it towards the company, our colleagues or our customers.

UOB Private Bank is a leading Asian asset manager with award-winning investment expertise in fixed income and equities. Headquartered in Singapore, we offer global investment management expertise to individuals, institutions and corporations from a regional network spanning Thailand, Malaysia, Brunei, Japan and beyond. Our comprehensive product suite includes innovative solutions covering retail unit trusts, exchange-traded funds and customised portfolio management services.

Company description:

About Hotelbeds Group

Hotelbeds Group is a business-to-business provider of services to the travel industry globally and the world´s leading bedbank.

The Group's proprietary technology helps providers of travel services distribute their offering to travel sellers globally via an easy-to-use, advanced technology platform that increases reach, revenue and yield for both the provider and the seller.

Operating mainly under the Hotelbeds, Bedsonline, Tourico Holidays and GTA brands, the company connects over 60,000 travel intermediaries across more than 135 source markets globally with travel providers in over 200 countries representing more than 170,000 hotels, 22,000 transfer routes and 16,000 activities.

Additionally the Group also operates a Destination Services division offering in-bound destination services, such as tours or transfers, in around 40 countries. The Group also owns several other B2B travel brands such as Pacific World (focusing on the MICE area), Intercruises (shore side cruise solutions) and more.

In September 2016 the company became independent under the ownership of Cinven and the Canadian Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB). In June 2017 Tourico Holidays became part of Hotelbeds Group, followed by GTA also joining the Group in October; both companies remain independent brands whilst they are being integrated into the Group.

The Group is headquartered in Palma de Mallorca, Spain and has 8,300 employees globally (including Tourico Holidays and GTA).
