At Mico New Zealand, we’re proud of our history of serving New Zealand communities for the past 76 years. Mico Plumbing and Bathrooms is New Zealand’s leading specialist supplier of plumbing and bathroom products to trade, retail and commercial customers with a reputation for quality and customer satisfaction. We are part of Fletcher Building, a diversified building industry company. With 68 branches and over 500 employees throughout New Zealand, we are the biggest name in plumbing and bathroom supplies. 

Our Mico Penrose store is a small but well-established branch providing trade solutions to a large and loyal trade customer base, residential solutions to home builders and commercial solutions to the local business sector.

The role

We have an exciting role, where you’ll join a stable and thriving branch and enjoy the variety and opportunities of working in a small and experienced team, within a large organisation. At our Penrose branch, we’re committed to improving our customer experience, and we want our staff to have the same passion.

Reporting to the Branch Manager, this is a varied and hands-on role that will see you responsible for counting stock and maintaining stock levels, liaising with suppliers, producing quotes. Working with other team members, you’ll sometimes also be involved in receiving and sorting incoming deliveries, picking/packing and dispatching orders for delivery, and on occasion, delivering to our customers. You may even be needed to work behind the Trade Counter, ensuring that your customers, who are made up of tradies, businesses and home-owners, are greeted with a cheerful smile and exceptional service. 

You’ll have the chance to learn our products, and this will give you the chance to progress in the branch, the business, and the organisation. Product or industry knowledge would be a real bonus, but we have heaps of great training materials, if you’re a willing learner!

About you

To shine in this role, you’ll bring a customer-focused attitude and strong work ethic to the business and be prepared to work closely and flexibly with the rest of our team. The ability to build rapport and relationships should be your strength, and your IT savvy will be a must.

There is manual handling required, and so you’ll need to be physically fit and strong. A full, clean, class 1 drivers’ licence is required, and a forklift licence would be a real bonus!

What’s in it for you

The job title is: Oral Health Therapist.Further details: Employment Type: Permanent Full Time
Position Classification: Oral Health Therapist Level 2
Remuneration: $84877 - $97709 + Super
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: REQ402130
Location: Broken Hill NSW


What you'll be doing

The Oral Health Therapy position aims to provide oral health assessment, diagnosis, treatment, management, and education for the prevention of oral disease to promote healthy oral behaviours to patients, and also includes restorative/fillings treatment, deciduous tooth removal and preventive services for children, adolescents and adults where the OHT has adult scope of practice.
 
Are you up for a new, exciting career path in the beautiful Aussie Outback? Are you ready for all the benefits of country living including no traffic, affordable housing and a lifestyle that supports balance and wellbeing? Then this is the position for you!  

Incentives

  • 5 Weeks Annual Leave
  • Salary packaging (pay less tax!), this includes Remote Area Housing and Meal Entertainment Card
  • Special rates at local gyms
  • A comfortable country lifestyle that supports balance & wellbeing

About Broken Hill

A true “Oasis in the Outback”, Broken Hill is a thriving regional town in far west NSW full of diversity, history and character. Being Australia’s first city to be Nationally Heritage Listed, Broken Hill is a culturally rich town with a vibrant art scene with over 20 galleries! The unique attractions, festivals and beautiful natural landscapes see tourists flock from all over, but the ones who stay quickly fall in love with the place and its liveability.

With a population just shy of 20,000, Broken Hill is small enough to allow for a relaxed country lifestyle, while big enough to provide all the desired facilities of a regional hub including major supermarkets and retail stores, excellent schools (7 primary & 2 high), multiple gyms & aquatic centre, well-known fast food franchises and a plethora of trendy restaurants, pubs and cafés.

The beautiful Murray-Riverina region is just 2.5 hours from Broken Hill, and after a short, 5-hour drive you can enjoy the beautiful Barossa Valley – South Australia’s internationally acclaimed wine region. For a town so unique, it’s really not that far away with just a short 1hr15m flight from Adelaide, a 2hr flight from Melbourne or a 2hr30m flight from Sydney.

Broken Hill truly is a town like no other with a supportive community that will welcome you with open arms. We can’t wait to see you soon!




Selection Criteria

  1. Registration with Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA - Dental Board of Australia) to practice Dental Therapy.
  2. Significant clinical experience in the provision of Dental Therapy to children.
  3. Relevant experience in oral health promotion and demonstrated commitment to evidence based health promotion targeting at risk communities.
  4. High level or oral and written communication skills and interpersonal skills.
  5. Demonstrated ability to work within a multi-disciplinary team.
  6. Demonstrated computer literacy to effectively utilise dental software packages (eg Titanium).
  7. Class C drivers licence and ability and willingness to travel for work purposes.

About the Far West LHD

The Far West Local Health District is one of 15 LHDs under NSW Health, providing high quality public health services to the communities in far west NSW. FWLHD has a mandate to provide the highest quality care and services to its communities using the latest clinical evidence and technological enablers. Our vision is to create excellence in rural and remote healthcare.

Key to our success of course, is our people. Our workforce is inclusive and diverse. We employ well over 800 clinicians and support staff across our 9 health facilities in Broken Hill, Balranald, Dareton, Ivanhoe, Menindee, Tibooburra, Wentworth, White Cliffs and Wilcannia. In the Far West LHD, we are working together to make a real difference to the health outcomes for our communities. We encourage you to consider joining our friendly team for a meaningful and rewarding career in rural and remote healthcare.

  2) Find out more about applying for this position
For role related queries or questions contact Karen Kennedy on Karen.Kennedy3@health.nsw.gov.au

The job title is: Senior Software Engineer - Motor Drives and Advanced Control.Further details:

Company description:

About us

At Dyson we are encouraged to think differently, challenge convention and be unafraid to make mistakes. We're creative, collaborative, practical and enthusiastic. But most of all we're hugely passionate about what we do.

Dyson offers a unique opportunity for talented individuals to invent, design and develop market leading products for the global market. By working in our world-class research, design and development (RDD) department, these individuals have the opportunity to work alongside leading technical specialists and highly motivated creative people to create products which fulfil our ambition of being truly different and better than our competitors.


Job description:

About the role

  • Develop and maintain real time embedded software for our world leading Dyson Digital Motors and other advanced control systems. Develop software for test systems to enable automated production testing including motor production line tune and test and power electronics hardware test. This will involve independent working and close collaboration with other team disciplines in UK and SEA on the implementation and modification of novel control schemes within the constraints of low-cost microcontrollers.

  • Contribute to software component development, driving their design, development, and validation though to mass volume production.

  • Support the MDAC software team through software validation to ensure that all released software is fully functional and fit for purpose. This will include code peer review, emulator validation and full system validation.

  • Document software requirements, design, implementation and test plans.

  • Support the software team through the software release process and change management systems through the preparation of high-quality documentation of either your own work or that of others.

  • Be responsible for embedded software aspects of failure analysis: completing root cause analysis of any failures of the motor or associated drive and control system at both product and motor level.

  • Be able to apply your skills to other areas of work and tasks within the business as may be required of you on occasion for the benefit of the wider team. This could include, but is not limited to, supplier liaison for issue resolution or audit, engineering design work, test rig building and production equipment commissioning.


What we offer:

Benefits

Dyson monitors the market to ensure competitive salaries and bonuses. Beyond that, you'll enjoy a transport allowance and comprehensive medical care and insurance. But financial benefits are just the start of a Dyson career. Professional growth, leadership development and new opportunities abound, driven by regular reviews and dynamic workshops. And with a vibrant culture, the latest devices and a relaxed dress code reflecting our engineering spirit, it's an exciting team environment geared to fuelling and realising ambition.

 
 

Required profile:

About you

  • Degree in electrical/electronic/software engineering or equivalent qualification or demonstrable experience of equivalent-level working.

  • At least 3 years professional experience in a relevant industry.

  • Strong background in real time embedded C and Python.

  • A good understanding of basic hardware and its interface with software systems.

  • Software configuration management (source control, continuous integration).

  • Ability to plan and estimate development tasks.

  • Experience with software verification strategies including unit testing.

  • Experience with triaging of issues/problems and narrowing down to smaller components.

  • Strong communication and team working skills to be able to form a bridge between multiple teams of different disciplines working on a single, integrated product across multiple global sites.

  • Be able to clearly report progress in meetings together with producing a high standard of documentation.


These are desirable but not essential

  • Knowledge of low-cost microcontrollers to enable the selection and integration of the most appropriate device for any given application.

  • Familiarity of low-level embedded microcontroller-based control and operation of brushless motors (e.g. permanent magnetic brushless DC motor, switch reluctance motor) and the topology of the motor drive hardware system to allow creativity in the implementation of motor control schemes.

  • Knowledge of control systems and power electronics circuitry.

  • Proficient in the use of LabView and Microsoft Visual Studio to be able to maintain existing and create new programs.

  • Experience of working in a matrix organization and within an Agile framework. Knowledge of Agile software development methodologies and tools such as GIT.

Calvary Mater Newcastle

The Quality Engineer is a member of an Agile Team responsible for testing software developed in Bangkok for our Capital Markets FX RFQ Product (FXall) The Quality Engineer will work as a part of a Scrum team to design and script test scenarios which ensure Product stories meet agreed Acceptance criteria. The Quality Engineer will be expected to provide both Manual and Automation testing and will help to build out Continuous Integration and Behavior Driven Development.

LSEG is an Equal Opportunities employer, we strive to establish teams that are diverse and encourage collaborative working and sharing of ideas.

This role is Digital First Hybrid, the successful candidate will be required to work from the office 1 day per week or 3/4 days per month.

Role requirements:

  • Work collaboratively with Development, Business Analysts, TPM’s and Product to ensure ‘Definition of Ready’ criteria are met and Acceptance Criteria are unambiguous for user stories.
  • Using BDD concepts, script, maintain and update automated test scenarios and test cases based on the requirement specifications and Acceptance Criteria.
  • Work with a team of 5/6 people in delivery of an Automation first “In-Sprint” capability.
  • This is an Automation role however there will also be a requirement to provide Manual testing.
  • Troubleshoot issues in automated test scripts.
  • Report issues and anomalies in the system in the issue tracking system.
  • Work with Product and TPM team to ensure defects are correctly prioritised.
  • Communicate risks to quality and testing schedules to QA Lead / Quality Manager.
  • Support QA Lead with test planning through provision of estimates.
  • Provision of metrics to QA Lead to support reporting and creation of QA project artefacts including Test scenarios, Test Scripts, Defect reports and Status reports.
  • Identify opportunities for improvements in QA tools and methodologies.

Key Behavior

  • Be comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where needs evolve rapidly and priorities change.
  • A passion for learning and innovation is critical.
  • An experienced software tester who has a passion for delivering quality.
  • You should be comfortable to challenge and ask questions.
  • Employ their multi-faceted skills to create imaginative solutions as well as coaching and nurturing excellence in others.
  • Be on the lookout for chances to call your team on to greater things, both individually and as a unit.
  • Interested in the evolution of the FX, Equities and Derivatives trading landscape.

Knowledge, Skills and Experience required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science/Engineering or related field or equivalent professional qualification.
  • Minimum of 3 years experience as a Quality Engineer in an Agile team..
  • Able to demonstrate an understanding FX trading.
  • Scripting test cases based on requirements using BDD.
  • Developing and building tests into automated test suites.

The job title is: Reliability Engineer (Mechanical & Electrical/Automation).Further details:

Reliability Engineer (Mechanical & Electrical/Automation) - 2 headcounts

Location: Chonburi

Job Summary:

The Reliability Engineer (Mechanical & Electrical/Automation) will be responsible for ensuring the reliability, efficiency, and safety of both mechanical and electrical/automation systems within our food manufacturing facility. The role involves developing and implementing strategies to improve the performance of all related assets, minimizing downtime, and optimizing maintenance practices.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and Implement RCM Strategies: Design and execute reliability-centered maintenance (RCM) strategies for both mechanical and electrical/automation systems.
  • Analyze Equipment Performance: Monitor and analyze performance data from mechanical, electrical, and automation systems to identify trends and root causes of failures.
  • Optimize Maintenance Procedures: Collaborate with operations and maintenance teams to refine and optimize maintenance schedules and procedures.
  • Lead Improvement Projects: Oversee reliability improvement projects, including upgrades, replacements, and modifications of mechanical and electrical/automation systems.
  • Asset Management: Develop and maintain comprehensive asset management plans, including spare parts inventory and lifecycle management for both mechanical and electrical/automation systems.
  • Troubleshoot and Resolve Issues: Provide expert technical support for diagnosing and resolving mechanical, electrical, and automation issues.
  • Ensure Compliance: Ensure all systems comply with industry standards, safety regulations, and food safety requirements.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in reliability engineering, preferably within the food and FMCG manufacturing industry.
  • Proficient in electrical systems, control systems, and automation technologies, including PLCs and electrical schematics.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills.
  • Good command in English

Argyll Scott Asia is acting as an Employment Agency in relation to this vacancy.

He kōrero mō mātou - About us

Community Living Limited is a leading provider of support for people living in the community with an intellectual disability.  We work alongside people with intellectual disabilities to design supports that meet their unique challenges, needs and the life they want to lead. 

About the role

  • We currently have full and part time positions in our rural Waikato homes, for morning, afternoon, night, and weekend shifts.  
  • We are looking for experienced and compassionate support workers to provide supervision, guidance, and practical supports for neurodiverse young men living intellectual disabilities and developmental trauma.

You must have a full New Zealand drivers’ licence and be a New Zealand citizen or resident.

Successful applicants will join a team that has a strong focus on providing positive outcomes for people.  Previous experience in the health or disability sector or mental health support work would be an advantage; however, training is provided to candidates with the right values and skills.

The job title is: Engineer/Senior Power Systems Engineer.Further details:

Transpower's Whakamana i Te Mauri Hiko outlines New Zealand's opportunity to electrify the country to help meet our climate change ambitions. To do this we are forecasting significant increases in both grid and local network connected energy resources. 

About the team

The Power Systems team's main focus is to provide power system engineering expertise, in particular to continually work at identifying, classifying and mitigating existing and future power system risks so that in our role as system operator we can continue to securely operate New Zealand's power system.

We work with closely with the Electricity Authority to prepare New Zealand for a carbon zero energy future, by helping evolve the Electricity Industry Participants Code (the Code) to accommodate new energy technologies, and with Asset Owners to: understand their assets capability and performance against the Code; investigate system events; commissioning and testing new or existing assets connected to the power system. We also manage the divisions event investigation, risk and assurance frameworks.

Our Operations division is involved in working with electricity market participants, transmission and distribution network owners, and asset owners for any energy resource with a capacity greater than 1MW. To ensure we continue to have enough capability available to meet the increase in demand for our service we must look to automation and continuous improvement!

The opportunity

As a member of the collaborative and supportive Power Systems Group, you'll love the varied work and fully utilise both your soft and technical skills as a pragmatic and customer centric power systems professional.

You'll work closely with other power system professionals to explore and communicate the challenges and opportunities that the transition to a 100% renewable electricity system will bring. Thinking broadly and using your well-developed analytical and communication skills you'll help us engage with the Electricity Authority and industry participants to make the required changes to the market, standards and the Code to enable a secure and reliable electricity system.

What will you bring?

Your experience may include working for a Transmission System Operator, Grid Owner or Engineering Consultancy, where you have honed your ability to understand, analyse and solve complex power system problems. In this role that experience will be tested as you consider the implications to power system operations, system stability and system security of an evolving power system with an increasing penetration of renewable technology.

To be considered your previous experience, application and cover letter will demonstrate:

  • a Bachelor's degree in Power or Electrical Engineering 
  • knowledge and experience with Power System Analysis Tools to support building dynamic power system models, performing load flow and time domain simulations; ideally DSA Tools (TSAT) or DIgSILENT PowerFactory
  • high level, real world analytical skills and exceptional attention to detail
  • an enterprise-wide view and have the curiosity to question and look beyond the obvious to seek alternatives
  • an innate ability to work with/lead a team through influence, to deliver technical projects
  • well-developed communication and influencing skills - both verbal and written.

Bonus points for one or more of the following; knowledge of the New Zealand electricity industry, the Electricity Industry Participation Code and commissioning and testing experience.

Why work for Transpower

Looking after our people is important to us. That's why when you join our dynamic Power Systems team, you'll be eligible for a range of employee health and wellness benefits and on the job professional development. 

An equal opportunity employer, you'll enjoy a family friendly and flexible working environment, shared learning and the diversity of thought which comes from our people of over 28 nationalities.

If you are a collaborative and team orientated Engineer/Senior Engineer, seeking interesting and meaningful work and the opportunity to be part of Whakamana i Te Mauri Hiko, please review the position description available via our careers site and apply without delay. 

Applications close Sunday, 16 May 2021, however applications will be reviewed as they are received, and you may be contacted for an initial exploratory conversation prior to the close date.

Due to current border restrictions, preference will be given to candidates currently residing in New Zealand with full work eligibility, or NZ citizens/residents returning home. Reasonable accommodation is available however, to suit your personal circumstances.

To apply for this job, please click 'apply now' or go to our job site and enter the job code 22262SK

United Overseas Bank Limited (UOB) is a leading bank in Asia with a global network of more than 500 branches and offices in 19 countries and territories in Asia Pacific, Europe and North America. In Asia, we operate through our head office in Singapore and banking subsidiaries in China, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, as well as branches and offices.

Our history spans more than 80 years. Over this time, we have been guided by our values — Honorable, Enterprising, United and Committed. This means we always strive to do what is right, build for the future, work as one team and pursue long-term success. It is how we work, consistently, be it towards the company, our colleagues or our customers.

About the Department

UOB Asset Management is a leading Asian asset manager with award-winning investment expertise in fixed income and equities. Headquartered in Singapore, we offer global investment management expertise to individuals, institutions and corporations from a regional network spanning Thailand, Malaysia, Brunei, Japan and beyond. Our comprehensive product suite includes innovative solutions covering retail unit trusts, exchange-traded funds and customised portfolio management services.

Job Responsibilities

With UOB Asset Management's push into the ETF market across the region, you are expected to play a major part in conducting ETF research, both in terms of existing ETFs available in the market which UOBAM may use within our robo-adviser or institutional investment solutions, as well as new ETF product ideas.

As part of the Investment Partnerships & Solutions (IPS) team in UOBAM, you would also be involved in the various functions of IPS, including managing our strategic partnerships with external fund managers, developing fund-of-funds solutions, as well as building investment solutions for our digital platform, UOBAM Invest.

All these functions would also require you to provide marketing support, from time to time, in the form of client presentations, webinars and providing written commentaries and articles.

Job Requirements

You should have a University degree, preferably in financial-related discipline, with two to five years of working experience. You should have a good understanding on financial markets, preferably across various asset classes and investment strategies. Quant knowledge and proficiency would be an added advantage.

Relevant working experience in areas of ETFs would be desirable. Other helpful experience includes fund selection, manager due diligence and fund-of-funds construction.

We are looking for an individual with a curios mind and a desire to learn. You should have strong communication and inter-personal skills, given the need to work with colleagues in different functions and across the region. You should also be self-motivated and a good team-player. Candidates with less experience may be considered for a lower grade.

Be a part of UOB Family

UOB is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions at UOB are based on business needs, job requirements and qualifications. Company Description

Outsourced.ph is a leading ISO certified Philippines offshore outsourcing company that provides dedicated remote staff to some of the world's leading international companies. Outsourced is recognized as one of the Best Places to Work and has achieved Great Place to Work Certification. We are committed to providing a positive and supportive work environment where all staff can thrive. As an Outsourced staff member, you will enjoy a fun and friendly working environment, competitive salaries, opportunities for growth and development, work-life balance, and the chance to share your passion with a team of over 1000 talented professionals.

The Senior BIM Modeler (Interior Focus) is a key player in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry, specializing in the creation and management of detailed digital models for interior spaces using advanced Building Information Modeling (BIM) techniques. This role involves collaborating closely with design teams to develop comprehensive interior BIM families and produce detailed documentation for construction projects.

  1. Advanced Model Creation: Utilize advanced features of Autodesk Revit to develop highly detailed 3D BIM models for interior spaces, including furniture, fixtures, equipment, finishes, and other interior elements.
  2. Interior Design Collaboration: Work closely with interior designers, architects, and other stakeholders to integrate interior design concepts into the BIM model, ensuring alignment with project requirements and design intent.
  3. Parametric Family Creation: Create custom parametric families in Revit for interior components, such as furniture, lighting fixtures, cabinetry, and decorative elements, to enhance model accuracy and flexibility.
  4. Detail Documentation: Produce detailed interior construction documents, drawings, and schedules directly from the BIM model, including interior plans, elevations, sections, and material schedules, to support construction and installation processes.
  5. Quality Assurance and Clash Detection: Conduct thorough quality checks on interior BIM models to ensure accuracy, consistency, and compliance with project standards. Perform clash detection analysis to identify and resolve conflicts between interior components and building systems.
  6. Model Coordination: Coordinate interior BIM models with architectural, structural, mechanical, and electrical disciplines to ensure seamless integration and coordination of interior elements within the overall building design.
  7. Software Expertise: Demonstrate advanced proficiency in Autodesk Revit and other BIM software tools, leveraging advanced modeling techniques, visualization capabilities, and parametric controls to create highly detailed interior BIM models.
  8. Training and Mentorship: Provide training, guidance, and mentorship to junior BIM team members on advanced Revit techniques, interior modeling best practices, and parametric family creation.
  9. Innovation and Research: Stay abreast of emerging trends, technologies, and methodologies in interior design and BIM implementation. Explore innovative solutions to enhance interior modeling workflows, improve efficiency, and elevate project outcomes.


Requirements:

  1. Bachelor's degree in architecture, interior design, engineering, or related field.
  2. Extensive experience as a BIM Modeler, with a focus on interior modeling and documentation in the AEC industry.
  3. Advanced proficiency in Autodesk Revit, including advanced modeling techniques, family creation, and parametric controls.
  4. Strong understanding of interior design principles, materials, finishes, and construction methods.
  5. Excellent communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams.
  6. Attention to detail and accuracy in model development, documentation, and quality assurance processes.
  7. Certification in Autodesk Revit or related credentials (e.g., Autodesk Certified Professional) is highly desirable.
  8. Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines effectively.


Work set-up: Hybrid (10x a month in the Outsourced Eastwood office)
Work schedule: M - F, 3PM - 12AM (can be flexible)

  • Are you super organised and process driven?
  • Do you thrive in a fast paced and creative environment?
  • Do you love fashion footwear and are looking for your next (or first) step in your fashion marketing career?

 We've got an exciting opportunity for a passionate, innovative, and super organised Creative and Marketing Assistant to join our in-house Creative team at our Support Office in Newmarket, Auckland. If you are looking for a hands-on role that will immerse you in the fashion retail industry, helping set up and produce photoshoots and organise content creation through to ensuring outputs are uploaded on time to the right marketing channels then read on!

Who are we? A New Zealand family-owned fashion footwear retailer who's been around since 1948. We have 40+ stores across 3 brands (Merchant 1948, Mi Piaci and Deuce) in both New Zealand and Melbourne, Australia. Our people are at the heart of everything we do, which means you can expect to have a supportive leader, grow in your role, be recognised and rewarded for great performance and receive ongoing training. One way we work to inspire others is via our charity, The Young Hearts Project, which supports youth to reach their potential through community programmes.

 What will you be responsible for?

In our fast paced, ever-changing environment, you will be responsible for organising and assisting with the photography of our e-commerce images, assisting with the set up and production of our seasonal campaigns and content creation briefs, including booking models, organising, sourcing and setting up props and locations, as well as co-ordinating post-production of imagery. You will be responsible for keeping accurate records of all creative outputs as well as the organisation, filing, naming & uploading of such onto various channels and interfaces. You will assist the creative and digital teams by compiling various outputs together for them to use on branded marketing collateral each week. You will also assist the broader marketing team on various projects as required.

  • Flexibility - the retail environment is ever-changing, and we need you to be too
  • Great time management skills - you can be relied upon to deliver on time
  • Alignment to our values - Accountable, Inspiring, Integrity, Inclusive, Innovative and Proactive

 What's on offer?

The chance to work with some seriously talented people, lots of employee benefits (your footwear collection is about to get a whole lot better!), an informal dress code, flexible working days, 'Dog Day' Fridays and the opportunity to get involved with our very own charity, The Young Hearts Project, supporting youth in New Zealand.

 Does this sound like you? Apply today!

You must be eligible to work in New Zealand to be considered for this position. No agencies thank you.

The job title is: Relief Educator.Further details:

For Children. For You. For Always.

Are you ready to do something that truly matters?

At C&K, our purpose is to make a positive impact on children’s lives. It’s what we’ve been doing for more than 115 years. Through evidence-based thinking, hard work and true compassion, we’ve built a trusted reputation as Queensland’s leading provider of early childhood education.

But times are changing, and so are we. And although we’re passionate believers that children come first, we know our people must come first, too.

Join us and find a better way with C&K - for children, for you, for always.

“This is what I enjoy about working with C&K; the staff truly embody the company’s purpose of nurturing and inspiring children to succeed in an ever-changing world.” - Mackenzee Nicolson – Assistant Educator, Gumdale C&K

Help shape the future of children in our care

As one of our highly valued Educators and Early Childhood Teachers with our relief team, you’ll nurture children’s curiosity, creativity and capability so they become confident lifelong learners.

Playing a crucial role at our centres by covering sick days, programming, extended leave and lunch breaks, you’ll use your skills, ideas and passion for education to create a safe, supportive and engaging learning environment for children and their families.

By working at different centres, you’ll broaden your skills and experience while being supported by kind, humble people and leaders who share their knowledge to help you learn, grow and achieve more than you ever thought possible.

In return for your dedication and care, you’ll receive above-award hourly wages based on your qualifications:

  • Educator/Inclusion Support Assistant: $34.73-$37.68
  • Lead Educator: $42.49
  • Early Childhood Teacher shifts: $60.59-$62.22

What you’ll bring

To thrive and succeed in this role, you will either have or be working towards:

  • A Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care, Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood) or Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care.
  • First Aid, CPR and Asthma and Anaphylaxis certification.
  • Valid Blue Card or Exemption Card.
  • A Police Check current within three months (or willingness to obtain one).

We would also love you to have:

  • A passion for achieving long-lasting, high-quality outcomes for children, their families and the community.
  • A commitment to ongoing education and training so you can keep growing your career and impact.
  • Flexibility with working hours and willing to travel between your local childcare centres and kindergartens.

Why C&K?

Every C&K career helps children belong and grow. We want the same for you.

Here are some things we hope you’ll love about working with us:

  • For Children.

Joining C&K means impacting a child’s life journey for the time they spend with us and long after they leave. By nurturing a love of learning in our play-based environments, you’re doing something that truly matters – for now and for life.

  • For You.

So much of what we do depends on you. We’ll set you up for success with a range of benefits, programs and opportunities to help you earn, be well and grow. And you’ll team up with people who value your dedication and care.

  • For Always.

At C&K, you’ll help shape the future of the children in our care - and there’s so much more we can do. We’re investing and working hard to find better ways, and as an Educator, you’ll be key to helping us set a new standard for our sector.

You’ll also enjoy other benefits:

  • Live, work and be well with our Employee Assistance Program for you and your family, plus health insurance discounts through Bupa.
  • Get a better deal! We pay above-award wages and offer salary-sacrificing options, so you pay less tax.
  • Our Referral program also awards you with $1000 for referring a successful candidate for one of our vacancies so you can be rewarded for supporting your team’s growth.

Join us and find a better way with C&K - for children, for you, for always.

The children, families and communities we support are wonderfully diverse. C&K benefits greatly from a team that brings together many different perspectives and experiences, and we’re proud of our inclusive culture. We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and people from all backgrounds.

All C&K employees are required to undergo background checks, including a police check.

This position qualifies for a Recruitment Incentive Package up to the value of $10,000 (pro-rata part-time/temporary positions less than 18 months), and a reoccurring Annual Retention Bonus valued up to $10,000 (pro-rata part time), under the NSW Health Rural Health Workforce Incentive Scheme.

This scheme recognises the role key health workers play in enabling the delivery of rural and remote health services, and aims to provide incentives over and above award entitlements, to attract and retain staff in these areas.

Packages may consist of family and compassionate travel assistance, an upfront Rural Recruitment Cash Bonus upon appointment, contributions to professional development, utility reimbursements and study assistance, in addition to relocation benefits and accommodation assistance.

To recognise ongoing service in this role, once the successful candidate has served a qualifying period, they will become entitled to a reoccurring Annual Retention Bonus valued up to $10,000 (as taxable income).

For more information, please discuss incentive options with the contact person for this role.

Employment Type: Permanent Full Time
Position Classification: Social Worker 
Remuneration: $67442 - $108612 + Super
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: REQ386497
Location: Broken Hill NSW

Hybrid working model considered

What you'll be doing

  • The AOD Youth Clinician works with young people aged 14 to 25, their carers and family in a case management and therapeutic intervention capacity
  • This involves specialist assessment, care planning, treatment, withdrawal management, referral services to people experiencing drug and alcohol problems
  • Work across the CMHDA and CAMHS multidisciplinary teams and participate in educational outreach work

Incentives

• 5 weeks paid annual leave per year
• Salary packaging (pay less tax!), this includes Remote Area Housing Assistance Benefits and Employee Meal and Entertainment Card
• Paid Allocated Day Off (ADO) Every Month
• Isolation & climate allowance
• Special rates at local gyms
• Support through advanced education & training
• A comfortable country lifestyle that supports balance & wellbeing

About Broken Hill

A true “Oasis in the Outback”, Broken Hill is a thriving regional town in far west NSW full of diversity, history and character. Being Australia’s first city to be Nationally Heritage Listed, Broken Hill is a culturally rich town with a vibrant art scene with over 20 galleries! The unique attractions, festivals and beautiful natural landscapes see tourists flock from all over, but the ones who stay quickly fall in love with the place and its liveability.

With a population just shy of 20,000, Broken Hill is small enough to allow for a relaxed country lifestyle, while big enough to provide all the desired facilities of a regional hub including major supermarkets and retail stores, excellent schools (7 primary & 2 high), multiple gyms & aquatic centre, well-known fast food franchises and a plethora of trendy restaurants, pubs and cafés.

The beautiful Murray-Riverina region is just 2.5 hours from Broken Hill, and after a short, 5-hour drive you can enjoy the beautiful Barossa Valley – South Australia’s internationally acclaimed wine region. For a town so unique, it’s really not that far away with just a short 1hr15m flight from Adelaide, a 2hr flight from Melbourne or a 2hr30m flight from Sydney.

Broken Hill truly is a town like no other with a supportive community that will welcome you with open arms. We can’t wait to see you soon!


Selection Criteria

  1. Recognised degree or qualification in health, welfare, or social science with a minimum of two years AOD clinical experience with eligibility for NSW registration/professional association where relevant). Or if no recognised degree or qualification, significant AOD clinical experiences of a minimum of five years.
  2. Demonstrated knowledge and experience in drug and alcohol clinical practices and treatment interventions.
  3. Demonstrated application of evidence based practice and critical thinking to advocate for and implement recovery oriented individualised person centred and trauma informed care to clients of the Drug and Alcohol service.
  4. Demonstrated commitment to work and partner with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander consumers and their families to enhance health outcomes.
  5. Evidence of participation in own professional development and commitment to maintaining competence and enhancement of skills together with willingness to apply and share professional expertise with colleagues and students.
  6. Demonstrated effective interpersonal skills including the verbal and written ability to communicate and consult with clients, family and/or carers and other health, community and welfare professionals together with intermediate computer skills including use of the Microsoft Office suite.
  7. Demonstrated competence in the use of electronic information systems and the ability to maintain accurate medical records utilising appropriate documentation and entering data related to activity in a timely manner.
  8. Current licence to drive in NSW

About the Far West LHD

The Far West Local Health District is one of 15 LHDs under NSW Health, providing high quality public health services to the communities in far west NSW. FWLHD has a mandate to provide the highest quality care and services to its communities using the latest clinical evidence and technological enablers. Our vision is to create excellence in rural and remote healthcare.

Key to our success of course, is our people. Our workforce is inclusive and diverse. We employ well over 800 clinicians and support staff across our 9 health facilities in Broken Hill, Balranald, Dareton, Ivanhoe, Menindee, Tibooburra, Wentworth, White Cliffs and Wilcannia. In the Far West LHD, we are working together to make a real difference to the health outcomes for our communities. We encourage you to consider joining our friendly team for a meaningful and rewarding career in rural and remote healthcare.

 About the Opportunity

  • Are you passionate about making a difference in the lives of older people living with mental illness?

Does this sound like the right fit for you?

You will be working in the community with older adults experiencing mental health issues who may be living in their own homes, with family, or in RACF.

You will be providing recovery-oriented, person-centred biopsychosocial care planning and interventions reflected in all aspects of your practice and service delivery.

You will have previous experience working with older adults in a health or community setting, including experience of assessment, care planning and interventions which are appropriate for and effective with older adults experiencing mental ill health. Are you a Registered Nurse, Occupational Therapist, Social Worker or Psychologist:

  • Enjoys working within a multi-disciplinary team?
  • Wants to work on weekdays? No weekend work

The role is also responsible for non-clinical tasks including participation in quality improvement activities, clinical supervision and participation in administrative responsibilities as required.  

Where You'll Be Working South Western Sydney is rapidly growing and is a great place for young people and families to build a life. We are close to public transport, a short drive to the beach and the natural wonders of the Blue Mountains and Royal National Park.

The area is growing exponentially with many major shopping centers, great entertainment venues and the development of Sydney’s new airport all located within minutes of new housing estates.

As part of the greater Sydney area, we have bustling metropolitan hubs as well as areas that maintain their rural heritage. It is an incredible place to explore with adventure or relaxation are at your fingertips.

application guide

.

Relevant qualifications as a Registered Nurse, Occupational Therapist or Psychologist currently registered with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA), or qualified Social Worker eligible for registration with the Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW), or CSU Graduates: Bachelor of Health Science (Mental Health).
  2. Demonstrated experience in providing evidence based, strengths focused, recovery orientated assessment and treatment for consumers of the mental health service.
  3. Demonstrated commitment to the philosophy and practice of consumer’s families and natural supports participating within the treatment process, as appropriate and in accordance with the NSW Mental Health Act 2007.
  4. Effective interpersonal skills, problem solving skills and personal resilience.
  5. Highly developed written and verbal communication skills and competence in the use of information technology systems.
  6. Ability to work independently and in consultation with the multidisciplinary team.
  7. Knowledge of and the demonstrated ability to implement the quality improvement process.
  8. Understanding of specific and complex needs of older people living with mental illness in the community.
  9. Applicants must possess an Australian C-Class driver's license (including P1 or P2). Those who hold a C class license (P1 or P2 included) from a state other than NSW must obtain a NSW C class (P1 or P2 included) license within three months of appointment. Learner's licenses are not permitted.

Make a meaningful difference with BlueCare

We’re looking for someone who wants to make the world a little better through small moments that leave big impacts. To build meaningful relationships and make a difference in the lives of others. 

An integral part of our big-hearted BlueCare team, as a Hospitality Officer you’ll be encouraged to grow, develop and feel empowered to make the everyday easier for the people we care so passionately about. 

Let’s make a meaningful difference, together.

What makes a difference for you? 

With a Blue Nurses legacy dating back to 1953, BlueCare is one of Queensland’s largest and most trusted not-for-profit providers of community and in-home care, residential aged care, disability services and retirement living. 

  • Flexible work arrangements to support work-life balance

  • Diversity and inclusive leave, offering paid gender affirmation leave and cultural leave options (paid and unpaid) for those who may celebrate Lunar New Year, Diwali, Ramadan, NAIDOC weeks and other significant cultural events
  • Career development opportunities with one of the most trusted community and residential care providers in Australia to challenge yourself, grow and make a meaningful difference  

Your part in our BlueCare team

As a Hospitality Officer, you will be driven, organised and take pride in your presentation and providing support to residents with the following task: 

  • Prepare, cook and deliver food in adherence with Australian food safety standards and dietary requirements of our elderly residents

We encourage our team to be creative and enjoy themselves while contributing to our success. Come join one of the most trusted community and residential care providers in Australia.

What makes a difference for us? 

  • Prior hospitality experience in kitchen or cleaning
  • Enthusiasm and strong self-motivation
  • Great communication skills and excellent attention to detail
  • NDIS Workers Screening Clearance or willingness to obtain
  • Confidence to satisfy the relevant probity checks required by legislation or policies.

BlueCare is proudly part of the UnitingCare Family, we’d love you to be too

With more than 16,500 staff and 9,000 volunteers across our brands of BlueCare, Lifeline, ARRCS, The Wesley Hospital, Buderim Private Hospital, St Stephen’s Hospital, and St Andrew’s War Memorial Hospital, you are part of something bigger. Our team are compassionate, inclusive and committed to the work we do, helping people live life in all its fullness.

Start making a difference today

Our application process takes less than 15 minutes – Click the ‘APPLY’ button to be taken to our online application process and upload your resume and cover letter. Our team are available to answer any questions you may have. 

Diversity & Inclusion 

Our approach is simple –everybody is welcome here.  At UnitingCare, diversity is at the core of our who we are, our mission and our values. We are committed to providing equal opportunities to all employees no matter their sex, race, culture, sexual orientation, disability or gender identity. Demonstrating our commitment to reconciliation and building long-term employment opportunities for First Nations peoples, UnitingCare strongly encourages Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants for this position.  

Safe workplace 

We work hard to make our services welcoming and safe for every person. We are united in keeping children, young people and the elderly safe from harm, within our services, workplaces and the communities we support. We are committed to speaking up loudly for their safety.

•    A workplace culture with a foundation that promotes person centred care approaches and staff wellbeing 
•    Orientation and supported transition into your new role
•    Targeted clinical stream education programs affiliated with university partners 
•    Development pathways that are aimed at career progression
•    Salary Packaging – up to $9k for living expenses + $2.6k meal & entertainment + novated leasing
•    Corporate health and fitness program
•    Inner city location with direct access to eastern suburbs beaches, restaurants and transport links that are right at the front door 
•    Established partnerships with Universities that promote cutting edge research in wellbeing, education and teaching. 

Where you'll be working

Prince of Wales Hospital is a 440 bed tertiary referral facility with specialties unique to this campus such as hyperbaric medicine, acute spinal cord injuries and interventional neuroradiology. Each year we support approximately 25,000 emergency presentations, 2,500 operations and thousands of outpatient treatments. We provide a 24 hour Emergency Department (ED) supported by an Intensive Care Unit and pioneering telehealth facilities in stroke and COVID-19, to connect the team in Randwick with specialists across NSW Health.A new Acute Service Building will be opening early 2023 with state of the art modern facilities aimed at providing an exceptional staff experience and enhanced patient and family outcomes as a result of the provision of person centred care. 

Randwick Local council is renowned for our world-class beaches and supported by cafes and restaurants to tickle your taste-buds, Randwick’s fascinating coastline and atmosphere will have you in awe the minute you arrive. Offering a mix of historic buildings, impressive beaches and coastal walks coupled with boutique restaurants, transport links and a vibrant nightlife, you’ll never be short of things to do in this progressive community.


What you'll be doing

The vision for South Eastern Sydney Local Health District (SESLHD) is ‘exceptional care, healthier lives’. SESLHD is committed to enabling our community to be healthy and well, and to providing the best possible compassionate care when people need it.

South Eastern Sydney Local Health District (SESLHD) is committed to improving the care provided to our patients in line with our vision of Working together to improve the health and wellbeing of our community.  All staff are expected to act as an appropriate and effective role model and promote culture and supporting practices that reflect the NSW Health CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Respect and Empowerment through demonstrated behaviours and interactions with patients, clients and employees.

As a Registered Nurse, you will be dedicated to providing exceptional care and working collaboratively to achieve the best possible outcomes for patients. You’ll utilise your clinical knowledge and skills and relationship-building skills in practice, always demonstrating the core nursing values that supports person-centred care, such as collaboration, openness, respect and empowerment in every interaction.

Employment of a temporary visa holder may only occur if no suitable permanent resident or citizen of Australia has been identified for this position following suitable labour market testing.

All NSW Health workers are required to have completed a primary course of a COVID-19 vaccine which has been approved or recognised by the Therapeutics Goods Administration (TGA). Additionally, Category A workers are required to receive a booster dose three months after completing the primary course of COVID-19 vaccinations. New applicants must have completed the vaccination course prior to commencement with NSW Health, or provide an approved medical contraindication certificate (IM011 immunisation medical exemption form) certifying the worker cannot have any approved COVID-19 vaccines available in NSW.

Acceptable proof of vaccination is the Australian Immunisation Register (AIR) Immunisation History Statement or AIR COVID-19 Digital Certificate. Booster doses are highly recommended for all health care workers who have completed the primary course of COVID-19 vaccinations.

SESLHD is committed to creating a workplace that reflects the diversity of our community. This will help ensure our employees, our patients and their carers, feel supported. We encourage people from different backgrounds to apply.

Support for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander candidates
We welcome applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander candidates and we have an Aboriginal Employment Consultant that can provide support. If you have any questions or would like guidance on the recruitment process, please contact the SESLHD Aboriginal Employment Team via email to: SESLHD-AboriginalWorkforce@health.nsw.gov.au


Selection Criteria

  1. Current registration as a Registered Nurse with the Nursing & Midwifery Board of Australia.
  2. Demonstrated high level written and verbal communication, interpersonal skills and the ability to identify key messages, issues and concerns when communicating with others.
  3. Demonstrated ability to proactively engage with patients/clients to enhance service delivery and to guide others in providing service excellence.
  4. Demonstrated ability to work as part of a multi-disciplinary team and apply professional and ethical boundaries when dealing with complex situations.
  5. Basic computer skills and proven ability to use health information systems.
  6. Detailed knowledge and understanding of risk management, safety and quality principles and the role of the Registered Nurse in applying these principles.
  7. Demonstrated recent extensive post registration experience in an Acute Aged Care setting.

  2) Find out more about applying for this position

Applications Close: 25th January, 2023

Summerset Boulcott is looking for exceptional Caregivers to join our Memory Care Unit in our brand-new village. This represents an amazing opportunity to help shape the Village's exciting future. 

About Summerset: 
Summerset is the second largest retirement village operator in New Zealand. We're passionate about providing quality service to our clients and we are growing quickly, with 39+ villages from Whangarei down to Dunedin. We are proud of our dynamic work environment and an equally diverse workforce. 

Our picturesque Summerset Boulcott is a brand-new village & sits adjacent to the beautiful Boulcott’s Farm Heritage Golf Club, offering stunning views of the surrounding valley and lush greens. This village is still in development - once complete, this stunning village will offer a range of modern, high quality living & care options to our residents. 

 

About the Role: 
With our Memory Care Unit opening first, we are looking for experienced, passionate and supportive Caregivers to join our team. Once complete, this village will offer a range of modern, high quality care options to our residents, which means you will have the opportunity to work in different areas i.e. our Care Centre facility.  

This is a busy and diverse role, assisting residents with their day-to-day activities such as showering, delivering meals and much more. Therefore, you will need to be resilient, kind and patient, while a good level of fitness will prove useful for delivering the best in personal care. We are anticipating a start date of 4th June 2024 for this role. 

This is a casual contract on when required basis. 

Your responsibilities will include: 

  • Providing personal care to residents under the guidance and direction of the Registered Nurse 
  • Working as part of a team to support creating an enjoyable and safe home for residents 

 

About you: 
You will be a passionate & qualified Caregiver with genuine compassion for all kinds of people from all walks of life. To be a successful you will bring: 

  • Experience in aged care and or have a qualification relevant to the role 
  • Be a team player and be able to manage your time well in order to complete all your tasks. 
  • The ability to work on a rostered and rotating shift pattern (including mornings, afternoon and weekends).  

 

Summerset Boulcott offers a dynamic and modern workplace alongside an exceptional environment – unmatched in the Hutt Valley and Petone! So what is in it for you? To recognise the important work that you do for our residents, we offer: 

  • An enthusiastic and supportive team that is fun to be part of 
  • $25.39-$29.95 per hour based on your experience and or qualifications 
  • Weekend rates of an additional 40 percent of the hourly rate 
  • We offer career progression and support for those looking to develop their skills further in the aged care industry. 

If you, or someone you know, are strong enough to care, then we would love to hear from you.  

Due to NZ Immigration requirements, we are obliged to consider candidates that already have the right to work in NZ for this role first. Due to this we may not be able to support a visa application for this role. This role may close early due to an increased number of applications - apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment! 

The safety of our residents and staff is important to us. For this reason, we require all our employees to be fully vaccinated and boosted against Covid-19 before commencing work at Summerset. 

Please note, only suitable applicants will be contacted.

The job title is: Psychologist.Further details: Help shape the future of Education

He mea tārai e mātou te mātauranga kia rangatira ai, kia mana taurite ai ōna huanga

We work to shape an education system that delivers equitable and excellent outcomes

At Te Tāhuhu o te Mātauranga | Ministry of Education, we work to provide services and support nationally, regionally and locally to the education sector, and in some cases, directly to ākonga and whānau.

We shape the policies, settings and performance of the education system for early learning, schooling and tertiary.

We are making significant changes to how we deliver our purpose.

So that we:

  • Take practical action to give effect to te Tiriti o Waitangi.

  • Give priority to regional and local voice.

  • Deliver greater responsiveness, accessibility and integrated services and support.

  • Improve feedback loops and information flows.

Our organisation is made up of talented and committed people around Aotearoa, from a wide range of backgrounds and cultures. While we work in different groups and on different things, we all strive every day to make the biggest difference we can for our ākonga in our education system.

Mō tēnei tūranga | About this role

As a Psychologist you will play a critical role in our region's Learning Support team by;

  • Enhancing inclusive practices in early learning services, schools and other educational settings
  • Providing professional support and guidance to schools, teachers and families and building the capacity of those who are best placed to support the learning of children and young people
  • Providing appropriate specialist assessment and analysis for collaboratively planned, evidence informed interventions
  • Working as part of a trans-disciplinary team where a child''s needs are complex.
  • There may also be opportunities for involvement in project work, as well as individual casework, targeted (group) work, and universal (systems level) work
  • ‘Thinking outside the box'' and collaboration with others is encouraged, to ensure positive outcomes for students.

Salary range: $82928.00 - $117928.00 per annum + 3% kiwi saver. The successful candidate will be appointed at a salary which reflects individual skills and experience.

For more details about the role, you can view the job description here.

We also offer:

  • Flexible working arrangements where everyone feels valued & supported.
  • The ability to purchase extra days leave.
  • A range of employee network groups.
  • An inclusive environment that encourages your personal cultural competency journey.
  • Development and learning, including mentorship programmes and internal secondments.
  • Wellness initiatives to support your overall health and wellbeing.

Mōhou ake | About you

You will be a New Zealand Registered Psychologist under the Health Practitioners Competency Assurance Act and hold a current practicing certificate. You will have a master's level tertiary qualification and a post-graduate Diploma in Educational Psychology or equivalent.

You will also have / be able to demonstrate:

  • The ability to develop and interact effectively with people of other cultures focusing or relationship and recognising their identity, language and culture as a source of strength.
  • To demonstrate knowledge of, or a willingness to gain an understanding of Te Ao Māori and promote tikanga and Te Reo Māori.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills and an ability to work effectively with ākonga, whānau and Kaiako across a diverse range of settings.
  • Ability to translate practitioner knowledge into practical information to upskill the adults around a child.
  • Ability to co-ordinate service provision in a multi-agency, trans-disciplinary setting.
  • A full current driver's licence is essential. Travel across the district is a requirement of the role.

Mātau rōpū ake | About our group, and team

Learning Support is a critical part of the Te Mahau | Te Tai Runga (South) Group in the Ministry. We ensure that children and young people with additional learning needs are supported to achieve their full potential through education. Our Learning Support specialists work closely with families, whānau, caregivers, schools and early childhood educators in English and Māori medium settings and other agencies to help maximise learning outcomes and promote social inclusion.

Our specialists tell us they value:

• "The ability to make a positive difference in the lives of children, young people and their whānau and contribute to system wide change is a huge plus"

• "The Ministry offers a strong community of practice and the support of a large organisation, so I never feel isolated or alone"

• "I really value the ability to work closely with specialists from other disciplines. It enhances my own practice and thinking".

To learn more about Learning Support, the roles we offer, frequently asked questions, and more, click here.

Kua rite koe mō tēnei mahi? | Are you ready to make a difference?

We are committed to reflecting the diverse communities we serve, and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, orientations, and identities.

If this opportunity interests you, please submit your cover letter and resume by using the ‘apply' button (applications via email will not be accepted). In your cover letter we'd like to know about you, your values, or anything else you'd like to share. We're keen to understand your motivations, strengths, transferable skills, and the diverse perspectives you will bring to the role.

For further information, please contact Nicole Wilkinson - Service Manager at nicole.wilkinson@education.govt.nz - 03 455 3758.

Applications close Midnight - Sunday 03 December 2023.

We want our people to feel valued for their unique qualities and have a sense of belonging. If you require assistance or adjustments to fully participate in the recruitment process, please let us know.

Our client, a global luxury retailer, is seeking a highly skilled and experienced Business Analyst(Assistant Manager) to join their team. As a key contributor to the organization, you will be responsible for business process optimization and driving operational excellence. If you have 5+ years of experience in ERP, a strong understanding of supply chain flows and processes, and expertise in utilizing Power BI for data analysis, this is an exciting opportunity to make a significant impact in the retail, e-commerce, and data analytics domains.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead business process optimization initiatives, collaborating with cross-functional teams to identify areas for improvement and efficiency gains.
  • Utilize your expertise in ERP systems to streamline operations, enhance workflows, and ensure seamless integration across different business functions.

  • Leverage Power BI reports and data analysis techniques to generate actionable insights, drive data-driven decision-making, and support business growth.
  • Take ownership of various projects, including retail expansion, e-commerce optimization, and data analytics initiatives.
  • Collaborate closely with stakeholders at all levels of the organization to gather requirements, define project objectives, and ensure successful project delivery.
  • Stay up-to-date with industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices related to retail, e-commerce, and data analysis, integrating them into business strategies.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, or a related field. An advanced degree is a plus.
  • Proven track record of at least 5 years in a Business Analyst role with a focus on business process optimization, preferably within the luxury retail industry.
  • With managerial and supervisory experience is highly preferable

  • In-depth experience working with ERP systems, effectively utilizing their capabilities to optimize business processes.
  • Proficiency in Power BI or similar tools for data analysis and reporting.
  • Project management skills, with the ability to handle multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.

Joining our client's team as a Business Analyst(Assistant Manager grade) offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the success of a global luxury retailer and shape the future of their business processes.

About Toll Group

At Toll, we do more than just logistics - we move the businesses that move the world. Our 16,000 team members can help solve any logistics, transport, or supply chain challenge - big or small. Toll has an expanding Defense aviation support portfolio including maintenance and flight operations in support of ADF capability.

For more information about our client operations and training facility please refer to https://www.linkedin.com/company/toll-ambulance-rescue and www.linkedin.com/company/ace-training-centre

Job Description

We have a unique opportunity to join Toll Group in our Helicopters business as an Aviation Stores Logistics Officer based in Bankstown. The Aviation Stores Logistics Officer will be responsible for the Supply Chain, Stores and Logistics of Toll Helicopters Equipment, Spare Parts and Consumable inventory. This function will support in the safety and availability of the Toll Helicopters fleet of aircraft by pre locating equipment and spares at various locations for use.

This role will be working a shift pattern of 8:6.

  • Manage the timely actions of the Toll Helicopters Supply Chain including Aviation and commercial stores, Logistics of Equipment, Spare Parts and Consumable inventory to ensure Helicopter availability is maximised and records are accurate
  • Self-Supervise and bring to the attention of the relevant maintenance manager of non-compliance with Toll Helicopter Policy and Procedure issues
  • Ensure any maintenance requiring specialist services is carried out by suitably qualified suppliers
  • Complete the documentation records correctly
  • Show initiative, persistence and continuous improvement in all processes
  • Knowledge of CASA and WHS regulatory requirements & processes as they pertain to aircraft and safety


Qualifications

  • Possess good communication skills and conflict resolution skills.
  • Possess good technology skills to operate the company ERP system.
  • Be medically fit, to be able to lift and move heavy inventory items and work in confined spaces and at heights on platforms around aircraft and in vehicles.
  • Be able to concentrate and have an attention to detail in all work (this work is responsible for public safety) A highly organized and systematic person.
  • A trade background would be desired.
  • Work effectively and flexibly within available time.
  • Previous experience working within a warehouse environment would be desired.

What moves you?

At Toll, you can help play a vital role in delivering what matters. From food, fuel, medicine and rescue services, we keep businesses and communities thriving. Every day brings change. We see that as an opportunity. To be curious. To ask the right questions. And build meaningful connections. Because finding new ways to solve problems is what we do. At Toll everyone is welcome including those of all ages, ethnicities, genders and abilities.

To find out more about us visit www.careers.tollgroup.com

The job title is: General Sales Manager.Further details:

General Sales Manager

Discover a rewarding career as a General Sales Manager at Darwin Motor Group.

THE ROLE

The largest automotive dealership in Darwin is now seeking an energetic hands-on style General Sales Manager to join our team and assist the Dealer Principal in driving the business towards continued growth.

With the encumbered GSM moving to Victoria for family reasons, he has given ample notice and it is envisaged that there would be an orderly hand over period for the incoming GSM.

With a focus on lifestyle and professional development, this role offers an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic environment. With amazing areas around Darwin to explore, that the whole family can enjoy.

As the General Sales Manager, you will be overseeing and working with four sales managers who collectively manage eight prestigious brands. While the sales managers possess their own expertise, your primary responsibility as the GSM will be to coach and mentor them, consistently improving their performance. This includes guiding them in such areas as stock management, staff training and development, P&L controls, OEM reporting and compliance, OEM target achievement. 

Reporting to the Dealer Principal, who has made significant improvements to the dealership and is committed to the ongoing improvement of the customer experience. You to work closely with the Dealer Principal and occasionally act on their behalf when required. You will be responsible for overseeing all new vehicle operations and providing daily and monthly reports to the Dealer Principal.

To excel in this position, you should have at least 2 years’ experience as a GSM or Senior Sales Manager managing multiple brands and locations. With a strong background in retail and fleet is essential, along with the ability to effectively manage new car stock to maximize factory incentives and control aging stock. Your knowledge and expertise will be instrumental in mentoring, coaching, and developing the sales managers under your supervision.

WHY US:

Darwin Motor Group is a proud member of the Pickering's Automotive Group a family-owned business that started in Townsville in 1978. with 21 new car brands in eight cities across Queensland and the Northern Territory. The group is ranked 14th largest private retailer and 4th biggest private automotive group in Australia. Our success is built valuing our staff and providing them with continuous access to training and the latest in technology. 

Our size allows us to offer unparalleled support to our employees. We have an in-house IT team dedicated to training you on our software and ensure you are not wasting hours waiting on external helplines. Or HR department ensures legal compliance, freeing up local managers to focus on supporting their teams. With a strong in-house marketing team who will maximize your advertising dollar to create an ever-growing customer base.

What is on Offer?

Very competitive remuneration package with a retainer and a commission structure. Successful candidates can expect an OTE of $160000 to $180000 per year.

You will also enjoy a company car or car allowance,

Assistance with relocation

Short term support with rental accommodation to help you to settle in quickly and focus on your responsibilities.

Long term career opportunity with genuine prospects career advancement.

The Darwin Lifestyle

Darwin is a laid-back relaxed city with a great family-friendly lifestyle and a very stable economy. With a thriving government hub and plans for significant growth in the next 5 years, as well as a bustling international port, Darwin stands at the heart of the Northern Territory’s natural beauty and tourism industry. The Northern Territory has traditionally been the second most popular destination for domestic tourism. 

With just 2 seasons the wet season and the dry season, you can enjoy a warm climate all year round. To explore the amazing surrounds, and breathtaking sunsets, a unique feature of Darwin, provide the perfect pause after a busy day. As the only Australian city with a CBD that faces West over our beautiful harbour Darwin offers stunning sunsets, especially during the wet seasons when the mesmerizing electrical storms roll in. 

Community Focused

We also believe in giving back to our local communities by supporting the local arms of three national charities, including, NT Autism, NT Down Syndrome Kids and the NT Cancer Council, along with a selection of the local sporting clubs.

ABOUT YOU 
Above all else, you are ready for a fast-paced career as a professional General Sales Manager looking to grow your career into more senior roles as the opportunities present themselves.

With a desire to live in Darwin and explore all the Northern Territory has to offer.

Enjoy a warmer climate all year round.

Currently, working in automotive retail, with at least 2 years’ experience in a similar sized role

High level of computer literacy with experience using Microsoft Office and Dealer Management Systems

Knowledgeable in the Finance and Insurance and update with compliance in this space.

Proven history of delivering exceptional customer experience and customer engagement.

With a successful past of developing a strong and focused team committed to continual improvement and long-term dealership growth.

HOW TO PRIORITISE YOUR APPLICATION?

Part of Pickering's strength is our commitment to technology, and this extends to our hiring process.

We have a sophisticated and vigorous selection procedure which is managed by Go Recruit Automotive Personnel, which starts with an online application by simply clicking the Apply Button in this ad. We will then be in touch with you to discuss the position in detail and understand your career experience.

This process ensures that if, we offer you a position in our business, you can plan on building a long-term career with us. We choose our staff very carefully, support them properly and years later they are still growing with us.

Thank you for applying. We will be in touch.
